Name: White Widow
Description:
White Widow cannabis is one of the world’s most famous and popular strains and descends from South American sativa and South Indian indica plants. The original White Widow was created by the cannabis connoisseur Shantibaba when he worked at Greenhouse Seeds in the 1990s, and this Dutch strain won the Cannabis Cup in 1995, just after it was released. Seeds from this cultivar are still being produced and provided by Shantibaba through Mr. Nice seeds under the name “Black Widow.”

White Widow produces an extraordinary amount of resin; the plant becomes covered in white trichomes through flowering, which is how White Widow got its name. White Widow could be seen as one of the forerunners for today’s high-THC strains.

White Widow’s genetics have helped create many subsequent legendary strains like White Russian, White Rhino, and Blue Widow, but White Widow still reigns supreme in some cultivators’ eyes.

White Widow has an earthy aroma with an ammonia-like scent and hints of pine but, according to some, lacks the flavorful profile found in many of today’s strains. Those who are accustomed to popular fruity and tasty cross-breeds may be relatively disappointed in the taste of White Widow. Those who enjoy the taste of more earthy, herbal cannabis may enjoy this cultivar.
Growing:
White Widow is a hardy and resilient plant, resistant to mold, mildew, and common diseases. White Widow is suitable for new growers with little experience, and as long as the plant’s basic needs are met, it will produce average or above-average yields.

White Widow weed can easily be grown outdoors and indoors. However, an almost Mediterranean climate, with temperatures around 70-80 degrees Fahrenheit (about 21-27 degrees Celsius, will provide optimal conditions for White Widow to thrive.

Typical yields for White Widow are 22 ounces per square meter for indoor plants and 22-25 ounces per outdoor plant.

Height

When grown outdoors, White Widow plants rarely exceed 6 feet in height; they grow bushy and wide instead.

Humidity and Temperature

A Mediterranean climate with some humidity is optimal when growing White Widow.

Flowering

Expect White Widow to flower within nine weeks when grown indoors, and the plants are ready for harvest in early October when grown outdoors.

Name: White 99
Description:
White 99 is a sativa-dominant hybrid made by crossing two polar opposite parents: Cinderella 99 and The White. The potent hybrid cross has an average THC level of around 20%-25%, giving rise to the strain’s potency. Although this potent strain’s creators are unknown, it remains popular among recreational users. Recreational users often enjoy this strain during the daytime due to its ability to increase focus and creativity. This strain is more suited to more experienced users with higher tolerance due to its potency and the skill required to grow it.

Its cannabidiol (CBD) content is extremely low, with maximum levels of less than 1%. This makes the strain popular predominantly among recreational rather than medical marijuana patients.

White 99 has flavonoids to thank for its citrusy aromas. Users note pleasant fresh citrus flavors, including orange and lemon, and pine flavors on the exhale. It may be appealing to those who may not like the aroma or taste of other cannabis strains.

Although this potent strain’s creators are unknown, it remains popular among recreational users. Recreational users often enjoy this strain during the daytime due to its ability to increase focus and creativity. This strain is more suited to more experienced users with higher tolerance due to its potency and the skill required to grow it.
Growing:
White 99 isn’t the first choice for many novice growers; it can be slightly more on the challenging side to grow. And even if successful, it has relatively low yields. In saying that, this strain can be grown from seed indoors and outdoors, giving some flexibility to growers. The plant has distinct vibrant green buds with yellow hairs, making it a visually appealing strain.

Height

White 99 reaches between 2 to 2.6 feet in height when grown indoors. If grown outdoors, the plant usually grows taller, reaching upwards of 3 feet.

Humidity and Temperature

White 99 grows best at around 65% relative humidity. It also enjoys warmer temperatures, upwards of 68 degrees Fahrenheit at night and 68-86 degrees Fahrenheit during the day.

Flowering

The flowering period begins at approximately eight to nine weeks, and flowering lasts between 42 and 50 days. At this time, the yield, if grown indoors, is around 5.6 ounces per plant. If grown outdoors, the White 99 strain yield is significantly higher, around 10.5 ounces per plant. These yields are remarkably lower than many other strains, making it a less popular strain for beginner growers or those seeking bumper yields.

The timing of harvest is essential to maximize terpene and THC content. The harvesting time is around October, but milky-white trichomes on the buds tell you when the buds are ready to harvest. This is inconsistent with the signs on other strains, indicating their readiness for harvest with yellow trichomes.

Name: Wedding Crasher
Description:
Wedding Crasher is a delightful hybrid cannabis strain developed by Symbiotic Genetics by crossing the popular Purple Punch with the Wedding Cake strain. This unique combination of 45% sativa and 55% indica characteristics boasts a THC content ranging from 15% to 20%, making it an ideal choice for those seeking a balanced, uplifting high.

With a smooth vanilla flavor, sweet grape notes, and a hint of sweet berry finish, the Wedding Crasher strain is a treat for the taste buds. Its long-lasting effects make it popular for recreational and medicinal users, relieving chronic stress, pain, depression, and mood swings.
Growing:
The Wedding Crasher strain is an excellent option for those looking to cultivate cannabis, as it is relatively easy to grow and adaptable to various environments. This strain is suitable for indoor and outdoor growing, making it a popular choice among novice and experienced cultivators.

Height

Wedding Crasher plants typically grow to a medium height, making them manageable for most cultivation spaces. This characteristic is advantageous for indoor growers, as it allows for easier control of the plant’s growth and overall size.

One of the most appealing aspects of growing the Wedding Crasher strain is its potential for a moderate to high yield. This means that, with proper care and attention, growers can expect a generous harvest of buds from their plants. This makes the strain particularly attractive to those looking to maximize their return on investment in terms of time and resources.

Humidity and Temperature

The Wedding Crasher cannabis strain prefers a warm and humid environment for optimal growth. Maintaining the ideal temperature and humidity levels is crucial for the overall health and development of the plants. Growers should aim for temperatures between 70-85°F (21-29°C) and around 40-50% relative humidity during the vegetative stage. As the plants transition into the flowering stage, lowering the humidity to around 30-40% is recommended to prevent mold and other potential issues.

Flowering

The flowering time for Wedding Crasher plants is approximately nine to 10 weeks, a relatively standard duration for cannabis strains. This timeframe allows growers to plan their harvests accordingly and ensures the plants have ample time to produce potent, high-quality buds.

Name: Wedding Cake
Description:
Wedding Cake, also known as Triangle Mints #23, is an indica-dominant hybrid cross between Animal Mints and Triangle Kush. Some people claim it is a cross between Cherry Pie and GSC. Wedding Cake has high THC content, averaging 25%, sometimes rising to 27%. Wedding Cake is 60% indica and 40% sativa.

Wedding Cake has relaxing and euphoric effects, but novices should be careful due to its powerful psychoactive effects. Wedding Cake’s high THC content may make it helpful in managing chronic pain, insomnia, and appetite loss. Wedding Cake is said to have a sweet, peppery, vanilla, earthy, and lemon flavor profile.
Growing:
Wedding Cake is a relatively approachable strain (cultivar) to grow and does particularly well indoors with a “sea of green” (SoG) setup. For this method, it’s ideal to find a strong mother plant, take cuttings from it and plant the clones. Expect yields of between 18 and 21 ounces per square meter. Wedding Cake can be grown outdoors but requires a warm, sunny, and slightly humid climate more typical of tropical or subtropical climates.

Height

Expect Wedding Cake to grow to short or medium height, between 2.5 and 5 feet, or 30 to 60 inches.

Humidity and Temperature

As with most varieties of cannabis, Wedding Cake does best at a humidity level of around 50% during the vegetative stage. However, Wedding Cake may have a slightly higher humidity tolerance than other varieties. It is ideal to gradually reduce humidity to 40%, 35%, and 30% during the final two weeks of the flowering stage.

The ideal temperature for Wedding Cake is between 70 and 80 degrees Fahrenheit (21 to 26 degrees Celsius) during the day, reducing the temperature by 10 degrees to 55 to 65 degrees Fahrenheit (13 to 18 degrees Celsius) at night.

Flowering

Wedding Cake can take seven to nine weeks to flower. In the Northern Hemisphere, you can expect to harvest Wedding Cake around late September or mid-October, or late February to mid-March in the Southern Hemisphere.

Name: Trainwreck
Description:
According to popular belief, Trainwreck was created by two brothers in Northern California during the late 1970s. Some claim a trainwreck occurred near where it was first bred and cultivated, forcing the growers to get rid of their crops quickly. It is thought this is where the name Trainwreck originated.

Its origins are a mixture of landrace cannabis strains like Thai and Mexican sativas and Afghani indicas. It is an old strain, reaching back to the 1970s, and has an aura of mystery.

However, experienced cannabis users report needing a few hits to feel the full effects of this sativa-dominant hybrid strain when heating and inhaling.

This strain is known for its earthy, floral, and pine flavor and moderate THC levels of around 18%. Many also claim it has a spicy taste, a bit like pepper.

Because this strain has brain-stimulating effects, it can produce heightened feelings of paranoia among users. Be sure to consume Trainwreck around trusted friends who can help if the effects are overpowering.
Growing:
The Trainwreck marijuana strain is versatile, enjoying indoor and outdoor growing environments. It can be grown from clones or seeds in dry warmth. One important thing to remember is that trainwreck plants can grow extremely tall and bushy and must be grown somewhere they can reach their full potential.

Indoor growing environments can have high yields — up to 18 ounces of weed per square meter of planting. But outdoor plants tend to have even greater yields — up to 25 ounces per plant.

Late harvesting, this strain tends to be ready around the end of October or early November.

Height

Trainwreck can grow incredibly tall. These plants have been reported to grow up to 15 feet high.

Humidity and Temperature

Trainwreck enjoys a humidity level of 80% to prevent mold and mildew and grows best in a moderate climate. Though it has a high tolerance for a range of temperatures, the ideal temperature range for this strain is around 65 to 85 degrees Fahrenheit.

Flowering

Trainwreck has an average flowering time of eight to 10 weeks.

Name: The Original Z
Description:
The Original Z (popularly known by a trademarked candy name) is an indica-dominant strain (cultivar) bred from a cross of parent plants Grape Ape, Grapefruit, and a third unknown strain. It was developed by Dying Breed Seeds, a collective based in California.

The Original Z has eye-catching purple hues resulting from high concentrations of anthocyanins during the flowering season. The buds are tightly packed, a prominent feature of indica strains, and they’re covered in cloudy white trichomes responsible for the strain’s reported psychoactivity.

The name comes from the candy-like fruit flavor and sour citrus aroma inherited from its fruity parent strains. It’s well-known for its uplifting yet relaxing effects. Therapeutically, it’s primarily used to manage stress, anxiety, and depression. The Original Z typically has a moderate to high THC level of 12% to 18%.

The Original Z won first place at the 2015 Cannabis Cup in San Francisco and first at the 2016 Emerald Cup.
Growing:
Unfortunately, The Original Z seeds can be hard to come by and are often unavailable for online purchase. The easiest option for those wishing to grow their own Original Z plants is to buy clippings from a healthy plant to propagate clones.

The Original Z can be successfully grown indoors and outdoors as it doesn’t require as much space as some other strains.

Due to The Original Z’s preference for humid environments, growers should be mindful of common molds and mildew. The resinous trichomes of The Original Z provide some anti-fungal resistance, but good air circulation and trimming are essential when The Original Z is grown indoors.

The “sea of green” method can produce a high yield of The Original Z.

Height

The Original Z only grows up to 3 feet (30 centimeters) indoors.

Humidity and Temperature

The Original Z thrives in a hot and humid climate.

Flowering

The Original Z flowers between eight to 10 weeks and produces average yields. Allowing The Original Z to grow for 10 weeks before harvesting buds allows for more resinous trichomes and better flavors.

Growers wanting to bring out the purple shades of the buds should expose their plants to cold temperatures before flowering begins to upregulate anthocyanin production. Yields of around 13 ounces (370 grams) per square meter can be expected when plants are grown indoors, and 17 ounces (480 grams) per square meter when grown in a warm, dry outdoor climate.

Name: Tangie
Description:
The Tangie strain is a popular sativa-dominant hybrid strain. It was created by DNA genetics by crossing California Orange and Skunk #1. Its name is a nod to its citrusy aroma and its similarities to the popular Tangerine Dream strain.

Tangie is a popular strain for recreational cannabis use due to its high THC content, sitting at around 20% THC. In terms of CBD, its content is low, bordering on non-existence. Its cannabinoid and terpene content makes it a delightful strain for those wanting to experience a balanced euphoric yet relaxing effect. Tangie could be particularly helpful for managing anxiety, depression, and stress.

This strain can really pack a punch and is extremely popular with adult users. It was created by DNA genetics labs but was kept under wraps for some time. Many suggest that it is a nod to the popular ‘90s strain Tangerine Dream.

This strain has won many awards, such as at the Cannabis Cup, where it took first place some years ago. The Tangie strain is known for its uplifting yet relaxing effects and fresh, citrusy aroma. This strain is often used to cross with other strains to create other well-known hybrids such as Sour Tangie and 24K Gold. You’ll likely find it on the West Coast, Colorado, and Arizona, where its climate is optimal for growth.
Growing:
This strain can be temperamental and requires some extra love and care, making it a more suitable strain for intermediate to experienced growers to try. Like many sativas, the plant grows tall and slender. Tiny orange hairs cover the plant, which, along with high levels of trichomes, gives the plant, and its buds, a vibrant hue.

Height

Due to its dominant sativa genetics, the Tangie strain can grow up to 6 feet. It is not an ideal strain for indoor growth. Trimming the plant’s top promotes lateral growth regardless of where it is grown. Additional support may be needed for its long, slender branches that may become fragile, especially during rain, and at risk of breaking off.

Humidity and Temperature

This plant is best grown outdoors in soil rather than indoors or hydroponically. This strain prefers a warm, dry climate, and wet climates make it susceptible to mold and put delicate branches at risk of damage. Its ideal temperature is between 70-85 degrees, while it thrives in relative humidities of between 40% and 70%.

Flowering

This strain’s flowering time is between nine to 10 weeks.

Harvesting time is around October, but it can be a couple of weeks earlier, depending on the growing conditions. Growers can enjoy upwards of 500 grams of bud per plant when grown outdoors, slightly less if grown indoors.

Name: Tahoe OG
Description:
The Tahoe OG strain — also known as the Tahoe OG Kush strain — embodies the typical effects of an indica plant while having a slight sativa-like kick. Growers say that Tahoe OG is a phenotype of classic OG Kush. The best aspect of this strain (cultivar) is that it matures at around 10 weeks, meaning it grows fast enough to make it ideal for anyone who wants to harvest their crop quickly. It is said to have more sedating effects, making it ideal for managing stress, insomnia, and chronic pain.

Tahoe OG was created in the 1980s near Lake Tahoe, California. The plant is typically indica-dominant; however, modern cross-breeding has produced some slight variations, and some of these plants may contain more sativa genetics. Generally, most Tahoe OG plants are 90% Cannabis indica and 10% Cannabis sativa. The THC content is no higher than 21%, and very little CBD is found in this strain.

Some plants have bright orange pistils and lime-green buds. Tahoe OG has been described as having an earthy, citrus, and pine taste and aroma. Many users prefer this strain because it induces deep sleep and relaxation.
Growing:
Tahoe OG is an indica plant. Most indica plants grow half as tall as sativa plants and tend to be bushier. Therefore, Tahoe OG is an ideal plant to keep indoors, although it can be grown outdoors if that’s your preference.
Like most cannabis plants, Tahoe OG produces natural compounds that make it resistant to pests and diseases. However, taking extra care of this plant is essential because it grows rapidly. As a result, it may not get adequate ventilation if the leaves aren’t pruned.
From Tahoe OG, growers can expect 11 ounces (310 grams) per square meter. Indica plants often have smaller yields than sativa plants, but the good news is that Tahoe OG is fast-growing, and in the long run, you might have bigger harvests overall. If grown indoors, remember to provide the plant with regular feeding, water, and sun for the best yield possible.

Height

Tahoe OG can grow up to 48 inches or 4 feet (1.2 meters).

Humidity and Temperature

As with most varieties of cannabis, Tahoe OG does well at a humidity level between 50% and 70% during the vegetative stage. Keep the humidity low at 30%-40% when buds start to form.
Ideal temperatures are between 70 and 85 degrees Fahrenheit (21 and 29 degrees Celsius) and no lower than 60 and 70 degrees Fahrenheit (15.5 and 21 degrees Celsius) at night if these temperatures cannot be maintained outdoors.

Flowering

Tahoe OG flowers at eight to nine weeks. Most indicas typically finish flowering at about six to nine weeks.

Name: Sweet Tooth
Description:
Sweet Tooth is an indica-dominant hybrid made by crossing Hawaiian and Nepali strains. It’s a mildly potent strain with a THC level of around 17%. Because it’s 60% indica, it has strong indica effects. Sweet Tooth has been described as having euphoric, long-lasting effects and, depending on the phenotype, can be myrcene, pinene, or terpinolene dominant. This makes Sweet Tooth ideal for managing stress, anxiety, and depression.

Sweet Tooth is resilient from being a cross between three landrace strains – Hawaiian, Nepalese, and Afghani. Its origins are from Barney’s Farm in Amsterdam. Landrace strains are genetically pure, producing resins and terpenes in response to the demands of the environment they’re grown in.

Rest assured, this strain lives up to its name, offering both sugary scents and sweet tastes. As an indica-dominant strain, it produces highly relaxing effects, boosts your happiness, and helps you to sit back and tap into your creativity.

Sweet Tooth boasts mango, berry, and grapefruit scents alongside an undertone of woody and earthy aromas. A pleasant floral scent lingers long after removing the strain from the room, so it doubles as something to smoke and a natural air freshener.

The strain won the 2001 Cannabis High Times award and placed in 2002 and 2003, enhancing its popularity in the early 2000s.
Growing:
High resilience makes this strain easy to grow, making it a great option if you’re a novice grower. Sweet Tooth plants fight disease and damage caused by viruses, bacteria, and pests. They’re a photoperiod strain, which means they need a change in the light cycle to cause them to flower. If you’re growing indoors, periods of 12 hours of light and 12 hours of darkness are sufficient.

Sweet Tooth plants benefit from pruning and shaping. When grown indoors, you can expect a yield of 2-3 ounces per square foot (550 grams per square meter). Grown outdoors, you can expect a yield of around 5 ounces (150 grams). Sweet Tooth typically has a thick covering of trichomes found on the dense buds, stalks, and flowers that look like a sugar coating.

Height

Indoors, Sweet Tooth plants grow to a height of 80-90 cm, and when grown outdoors, you can expect them to exceed 1 meter.

Humidity and Temperature

A sunny, dry, Mediterranean environment is optimal for this strain. Aim for humidity levels around 65% during the growing stage, and then gradually lower this as you reach the flowering stage to around 30%. This is important as maintaining an appropriate humidity level can boost the plant’s yield, appearance, and flavor and reduce the chance of mold and bud rot. Lowering humidity helps as the roots take on moisture while the plant matures, evaporating through the leaves, thereby increasing the humidity levels.

Flowering

Flowering time is typically after eight to nine weeks, so you can expect a harvest time around September or October.

Name: Super Silver Haze
Description:
Super Silver Haze (sometimes shortened to SSH) was born through the careful and strategic cross-breeding of Northern Lights, Haze, and Skunk #1, three of the highest quality strains on earth. Looking at its genetic lineage, it’s no question how Super Silver Haze rose to be a highly sought-after and award-winning strain itself.

Super Silver Haze is a sativa-dominant strain with a ratio of 70:30 between sativa and indica. This balance of sativa to indica makes Super Silver Haze a popular strain for use during the day as it has uplifting and energizing effects. These effects make SSH helpful for managing anxiety and depression when used in low doses.

The tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) levels of Super Silver Haze are moderate at 20% on average, with cannabidiol (CBD) levels almost nonexistent at less than 0.2%
Growing:
Growing Super Silver Haze requires some experience and is not suitable for novice growers, especially those wanting their plant to reach its full potential. As is typical with most other sativa strains, expect Super Silver Haze to produce tall plants and provide ample room to avoid overcrowding.
Super Silver Haze thrives best in hydroponic growing conditions but can also be grown in soil. If everything goes to plan while growing, successful indoor harvests yield around 19 ounces per square meter, and outdoor yields 15 ounces per plant.

Height

Super Silver Haze can easily grow to be over 6.5 ft tall.

Humidity and Temperature

Super Silver Haze requires a hot, sunny, and balmy climate, which restricts the geographical locations suitable for outdoor growth. Mediterranean and tropical climates are ideal for this cultivar.
Retain relative humidity between 65-80% when your plants sprout as seedlings. In the vegetative stage, slightly lower down to between 60-70%. In the flowering stage, humidity should be between 30% and 40% to prevent mold from growing on your flower.

Flowering

Super Silver Haze flowers within 10-12 weeks when grown indoors. These plants are ready for harvest in mid-October when grown outdoors in the Northern Hemisphere.

Name: Super Lemon Haze
Description:
Super Lemon Haze is a popular strain created by Arjan of Green House Seeds. He began with his previous famous Super Silver Haze, which won three consecutive Cannabis Cups in 1997, 1998, and 1999. He carefully bred it in a three-way cross of Lemon Haze, Lemon Skunk #1, and Northern Lights #5. The result was a sativa-dominant hybrid with sweet lemon and tart flavors.

The buds of the strain have a speckled green-brown appearance and are covered with a dense layer of resinous trichomes. These trichomes produce a potent mix of cannabinoids, terpenes, and flavonoids that give Super Lemon Haze its unique flavor.

In 2008 and 2009, Super Lemon Haze won the High Times Cannabis Cup first-place award. In 2014 it won the Seattle Cannabis Cup for the Medical sativa category.

Super Lemon Haze has potent THC content delivering effects for around three hours.
Growing:
Super Lemon Haze is a relatively easy-to-cultivate strain. It can be grown indoors and outdoors; however, sativas are known for their considerable height, so a high-growth container is preferred when grown indoors. Additionally, a controlled indoor environment is recommended to take advantage of the complete terpene profile.

Mold is common in areas with high humidity and low water evaporation. Super Lemon Haze contains resinous trichomes on its buds, which make it resistant to mold by the Botrytis fungus.

A hydroponic setup is recommended for vigorous growth. This involves using a nutrient-enriched liquid for the plant’s roots and allows the roots to have maximum surface area for nutrient uptake. Trimming of foliage is also recommended to promote airflow and allow oxygen to reach the roots.

Height

Super Lemon Haze is one of the tallest growing strains. It’s a fast grower and can reach over 6 feet in seven to nine weeks.

Humidity and Temperature

Super Lemon Haze requires a milder climate, growing best at temperatures between 65 and 85 degrees Fahrenheit (18.3 and 29.4 degrees Celsius).

Flowering

Flowering time lasts between nine and 10 weeks. It has a moderate yield; for each outdoor plant, you can expect approximately 35 ounces. For indoor plants, you can expect roughly 28 ounces.

Name: Super Glue
Description:
Super Glue, known by some as Tacky Glue, is a relatively balanced hybrid strain, containing approximately 60% Cannabis indica and 40% Cannabis sativa genetics. It is a cross between the well-known Northern Lights and Afghani landrace strains. Despite its name and high level of THC, Super Glue is not related to Gorilla Glue.

The Dutch seed bank Seedism Seeds initially produced Super Glue. It is a successful strain that has won several awards, including:

First place for Best Hybrid in the High Times 2019 Cannabis Cup Nevada.

In terms of appearance, the flowers are capped by sticky white translucent trichomes that appear glue-like when dried, which is one of the reasons this strain is called Super Glue. It has orange-red pistils and green leaves coiled around the buds.
Growing:
The Super Glue strain can be grown indoors and outdoors.

It’s described as moderately difficult to grow because it requires regular trimming. Trimming Super Glue can be challenging for some because the trichomes are sticky due to the high THC levels.

You can’t purchase Super Glue seeds online, so you’ll need to use clones taken from cuttings of a mother plant.

Indoor-grown Super Glue plants typically produce yields of 400 to 500 grams of bud per square meter (14 to 17 ounces). Growing Super Glue outdoors can expect a yield of between 500 and 600 grams (17 to 21 ounces) per square meter.

If growing Super Glue indoors, you may want to try the “Screen of Green” (ScroG) growing method that involves growing cannabis plants horizontally, under, and around a screen. Its purpose is to ensure that all parts of the plant, including the lower parts, are exposed to sunlight and air.

Super Glue is moderately resistant to disease. However, it does contain a large cluster of buds that grow tightly together, which means it is susceptible to mold. To prevent mold from growing on Super Glue, make sure that all parts of the plant always have good airflow.

Height

As an indica-leaning plant, Super Glue is relatively short in height and generally reaches between 47 and 59 inches (1.2 and 1.5 meters) inside. Outdoors, Super Glue can grow up to 78 inches (2 meters).
Rather than growing tall, Super Glue grows bushy and wide.

Humidity and Temperature

Super Glue plants grow best in a relatively humid and warm Mediterranean-like climate.
However, it also shouldn’t be too humid because this can increase the chance of mold growing on the plants.

Flowering

Once ready, the Super Glue flowers are dense, large, and spade-like in appearance.
Generally, Super Glue flowers at eight to nine weeks are fast for a cannabis strain.
If growing Super Glue outside, it will likely be ready to harvest in late October (in the Northern Hemisphere).

Name: Sunset Sherbet
Description:
The Sunset Sherbet strain of cannabis is an indica-dominant hybrid strain (cultivar) with an 85% indica to 15% sativa ratio. Although primarily known as Sunset Sherbet, the strain is sometimes called “Sherbet,” “Sherbet OG,” or spelled as “Sherbert.”

The strain is a cross between the well-known GSC and Pink Panties strains, has THC levels of between 18% and 21%, and has very low CBD levels. This means you can expect to feel relaxed when smoking in moderation and have a deeper sense of relaxation and euphoria in higher doses.

The strain will make you feel uplifted and positive regardless of how much you consume. For this reason, the strain is popular among people who consume cannabis for medicinal purposes, like combating chronic fatigue, stress, and anxiety. The THC content and high levels of beta-caryophyllene make Sunset Sherbet a popular choice for chronic pain.
Growing:
Sunset Sherbet is a simple indica-dominant strain to grow due to its ability to be grown outdoors and indoors and the low maintenance it requires during the growing cycle. The biggest downside to this strain is its relatively low yield. Indoor growers report an average of 8 ounces of bud, and outdoor growers report around 11 ounces per plant.

Sunset Sherbet plants love a warm, Mediterranean-type climate, so if you live in an area with this climate, you’ll be able to plant them outdoors in a nice, sheltered spot. If this isn’t an option, you can easily create similar conditions indoors with the proper setup.

Height

Sunset Sherbet plants grow to a medium height between 30 and 78 inches and produce large flowers. When grown outdoors, they will grow to a larger size. During the growing cycle, they require little maintenance, whether grown indoors or outdoors.

Humidity and Temperature

Sunset Sherbet thrives in a warm, Mediterranean-type climate when they are grown outdoors. Alternatively, it is a great strain to grow indoors hydroponically. Unlike other strains, they grow best in more sheltered outdoor spots.

Flowering

When you grow Sunset Sherbet plants indoors, you will have a flowering time of approximately eight weeks, and when grown outdoors, you can expect to harvest your yield between late September and early October.

Name: Sunbomb
Description:
Sunbomb (popularly known by a trademarked candy name), aka Pink Sunbomb or Sunbomb OG, is a sativa-dominant hybrid strain of 60% sativa and 40% indica. It has moderate to high THC levels ranging from 20% to 30%. This well-balanced strain has potent, energetic, and calming effects, as well as a sweet taste.

Pink Sunbomb is the love child of a slightly complex three-way cross between DJ Shorts Blueberry and Headband, and then with Sour Diesel BX3 — also known as AJ Sour Diesel. Anesia Seeds created it quite recently to cultivate a strain with a high THC content, a sweet, fruity flavor profile, and powerful effects.  Its effects suggest that Pink Sunbomb may help manage stress, anxiety, and depression.

With THC levels reaching up to 30%, there is no doubt that Pink Sunbomb packs a powerful punch. This strain may be too intense for beginners. Having a genotype of 60% sativa and 40% indica, Pink Sunbomb strikes a nice balance between stimulating and relaxing effects.
Growing:
Pink Sunbomb has two phenotypes, which have different growth and flowering periods, as well as different yields. The phenotype with the bigger yield takes five to 10 days longer to flower but will provide yields of up to 21 ounces per 10 square feet when grown indoors, and this phenotype can yield up to 25 ounces per plant in an outdoor environment.
The Pink Sunbomb plant can be grown both indoors and outdoors. Indoor growing gives more experienced growers opportunities to use a hydroponic setup or the “Sea of Green” growing method to increase their yields.
Because some extra equipment and techniques are involved when growing Pink Sunbomb, it may not be the best strain to try if this is your first attempt at growing your own cannabis.

Height

Depending on the phenotype and whether you grow your Pink Sunbomb indoors or outdoors, you can expect it to reach between 4 and 7 feet tall.

Humidity and Temperature

To grow your Pink Sunbomb indoors, you must control the temperature and humidity levels. During the vegetative stage, humidity should be high, around 75%. Throughout the growing process, the humidity should slowly drop and be no higher than 50% by the start of the flowering period and down to 30%-35% by the last weeks of flowering.
The temperature should be kept around 70 to 75 degrees Fahrenheit throughout. If you choose to grow your Pink Sunbomb outdoors, it will thrive in a hot, sunny, “Mediterranean” climate.

Flowering

Flowering time is also dependent on which phenotype you are growing. The shorter phenotype, with the smaller yield, will flower in approximately 55 days, and the larger, high-yielding phenotype will flower around day 65. Outdoor plants will be ready to harvest by early October.

Name: Strawnana
Description:
The Strawberry Banana strain — commonly called the Strawnana strain — is a beloved indica dominant hybrid with a sweet, fruity taste and an almost hash-like, spicy smell. It is thought to be a cross between Banana Kush and the Strawberry phenotype of Bubble Gum.

The Strawnana strain was created by DNA genetics and serious seeds by crossing Crockett’s Banana Kush with the Strawberry variant of Bubble Gum. Based on this parentage, it can be considered to have origins in India and Afghanistan, among other places.

Regardless of its parentage, it’s much beloved as an Indica with a sweet taste and smell profile and is considered relatively easy to use for beginners. However, its high THC content can catch users off-guard, leaving them more affected than expected.

Some have found the marijuana strain to have a smooth, berry-like aftertaste, but the plant has a pungent odor that can be an essential consideration for some. It provides users with a slow-building high, making it advisable to use it in moderation and wait for its effects to kick in before taking another hit.
Growing:
The Strawnana cannabis plant has small- to medium-sized flowers with a tight and dense structure. Its leaves are usually light green with an almost yellow hue contrasting with bright orange pistils and a fuzzy coat of white trichomes. Some leaves may also have purple spots if the plant is exposed to colder temperatures while growing. The plant can be grown inside or outside.

Height

The Strawnana plant can reach a height of between 70 and 90 inches tall, reaching the higher end of the spectrum when grown outdoors and being a bit shorter when grown inside. It tends to have big yields, which can be optimized using several handy tips and tricks.

Humidity and Temperature

A low humidity of around 50% and a temperature of approximately 70 degrees Fahrenheit are ideal for growing Strawnana. Reduce the temperature slightly when the plant starts flowering to prevent the buds from rotting.

Flowering

If grown inside, the plant can take anywhere between nine and 10 weeks to begin flowering. Outside, it is likely to be ready for harvest in early to mid-October. In case you’re worried, there are ways to tell if your plant has been flowering for long enough to be harvested.

Name: Strawberry Shortcake
Description:
Strawberry Shortcake is an indica-dominant hybrid created by cross-breeding The White and White Wookie strains.

Strawberry Shortcake emerged out of Colorado, but the detailed history of the strain is unknown. Multiple cultivators have been credited for creating Strawberry Shortcake, such as Cannarado Genetics and The Jungle Boys.

The indica-sativa ratio of Strawberry Shortcake is not entirely known. Still, it has all the characteristics of a strong indica instead of a sativa-dominant hybrid strain, such as sedation and a feeling of being unable to get up (“couch lock”). This makes Strawberry Shortcake potentially very useful for conditions like insomnia and chronic pain.

Strawberry Shortcake has moderate levels of tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) that sit around 20%. The cannabidiol (CBD) levels of Strawberry Shortcake are almost nonexistent at 0.4%, with a higher concentration of cannabigerol (CBG) at 0.8%-1%.

Strawberry Shortcake lives up to its name with a strong and inviting aroma of sweet fruity strawberries. After use, you’ll have no question about how it got its name.
Growing:
Strawberry Shortcake is unsuitable for new growers and can be somewhat tricky to maintain.
First, the seeds are hard to come by, but if you manage to get your hands on some, you need to be cautious as these temperamental plants only thrive in optimal conditions. You must make an above-average effort to prevent mold and pests before harvest.
Strawberry Shortcake grows into a medium-sized plant. When harvesting, you can expect yields of 1-2 ounces per foot (indoors) and 15-20 ounces per plant (outdoors).

Height

Whether it’s grown indoors or outdoors, Strawberry Shortcake plants grow to 6 feet.

Humidity and Temperature

Strawberry Shortcake grows best in a slightly humid environment but always be on the lookout for mold growth.

Flowering

The flowering time of Strawberry Shortcake is relatively fast compared to other strains at just 46-53 days.

Name: Strawberry Lemonade
Description:
Developed by Barney’s Farm from a cross between the famous Strawberry Cough and Sour Lemon OG strains, Strawberry Lemonade is a balanced hybrid of 50% sativa and 50% indica. The strain’s THC content ranges between 18%-28% with low CBD and produces intense cerebral highs followed by bodily relaxation. Strawberry Lemonade may help manage anxiety, depression, and PTSD when dosed appropriately.

During the initial high, users often feel a burst of energy, which can be an excellent opportunity to work or play before the relaxing effects kick in. The late-onset relaxing effects mean that Strawberry Lemonade is considered to be best suited for use in the late afternoon or evening rather than in the morning. However, the effects of any cannabis strain (cultivar) can differ from person-to-person, so take these descriptions for the anecdotal reports they are.

Strawberry Lemonade flowers release an earthy strawberry scent with undertones of fresh citrus fruits when adequately cured. Grinding the nuggets releases a dank, hash-like odor similar to that of OG Kush. The smoke has been described as smooth and easily palatable, with a sweet flavor during exhalation.

Strawberry Lemonade won best sativa concentrate at the 2015 High Times Cannabis Cup awards in Denver, Colorado.
Growing:
Unfortunately for those wanting to grow their own Strawberry Lemonade, seeds are difficult to acquire. The best method for growing is to use cuttings of existing healthy plants to create your clones. In states where medical cannabis cultivation is permitted, dispensaries may sell clones from specific, popular cannabis varieties. Such an option can be ideal for beginner growers as it shortens growing time by cutting out the vegetative period, allowing the plant to go straight into a 12-12 light-dark cycle.

Once cuttings have been obtained, the plants are relatively easy to grow and are resistant to common types of mold and mildew. Strawberry Lemonade can be grown indoors or outdoors, and indoor yields an average of 18 ounces (510 grams) for every 10.7 square feet,  and outdoor plants yield an average of 14 ounces (396 grams) per plant.

The small to medium-sized flowers stick together in clusters reminiscent of cauliflower heads. Strawberry Lemonade buds are dense and indica-like, with small, tightly coiled, light green leaves. These are interspersed with orange and brown colored pistols. The trichomes have a cloudy white appearance, making the flowers look white when viewed from far away.

Height

Strawberry Lemonade plants grow to 4 to 5 feet (122-152 centimeters) and may need to be topped if you’re growing them in a confined space. Topping involves pruning the top part off the end of the plant’s main stem to prevent further vertical growth, which also encourages the growth of the lateral branches, making the plant shorter and bushier overall.

Humidity and Temperature

Strawberry Lemonade prefers semi-humid climates with temperatures between 70 and 80 degrees Fahrenheit or 21 to 26 degrees Celsius.

Flowering

Strawberry Lemonade has a flowering time of nine to 10 weeks when grown indoors. If grown outdoors, it should be ready for harvest in late October.

Name: Strawberry Haze
Description:
Strawberry Haze, also called Arjan’s Strawberry Haze, was introduced in 2005. This strain (cultivar) won first place at the Green House Very Important Smokers Panel in 2005. As the name suggests, Strawberry Haze has strawberry-smelling buds, for which it’s become well known. Strawberry Haze has been described as having an energetic, talkative, uplifting effect, making it ideal for managing stress, anxiety, and depression.

Strawberry Haze is typically 70% Cannabis sativa and 30% Cannabis indica. It’s a rare sativa-dominant strain created by crossing Northern Lights #5, Swiss Sativa, and Kali Mist. However, it’s pretty easy to care for and thrives when the roots are given free rein in the soil. Additionally, Strawberry Haze provides an abundant yield because it grows tall with long branches.
Growing:
Strawberry Haze is a sativa-dominant strain. While most sativa plants are known to grow tall, Strawberry Haze grows not only tall but also has long branches that stretch away from the plant. Therefore, if you’re growing more than one plant, you’ll need to provide plenty of room for branches to spread. When grown outdoors, the plant grows up to an impressive 9 feet (2.7 meters). However, when grown indoors, it won’t grow this tall.

Strawberry Haze is 70% Cannabis sativa and 30% Cannabis indica. It has a high THC content, and the buds are known for their strong strawberry aroma. When grown outdoors, growers can expect an excellent yield of 21 ounces (595 grams) per plant. When grown indoors, expect a lower yield. Cut the top off the plant’s central stem when it has reached an acceptable height to increase flowering. Doing so will make the plant bushier, allowing more leaves and buds to grow.

Height

On average, Strawberry Haze grows to 9 feet (2.7 meters) when grown outdoors.

Humidity and Temperature

Strawberry Haze prefers a semi-humid climate. Therefore, keeping the humidity around 40%-50% is best. Always reduce the humidity as the plant enters the flowering stage to prevent mold from growing on the buds.
The temperature should be between 68 and 77 degrees Fahrenheit (20 and 25 degrees Celsius). As with other sativa-dominant strains, don’t leave this plant outside when the nights are cold.

Flowering

Strawberry Haze will flower for 10-12 weeks. Most sativas finish flowering in about 10 to 14 weeks.

Name: Strawberry Diesel
Description:
Strawberry Diesel is regarded as an ultimate hybrid because it is a cross between two top-quality parents, Strawberry Cough and NYC Diesel. This hybrid strain (cultivar) contains high THC levels and no CBD content, making it perfect for muscle relaxation, although it can also feel uplifting. Some users also claim that it’s excellent for clearing the mind and potentially very useful for anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

Additionally, the Strawberry Diesel strain is renowned for helping with insomnia. However, it’s not limited to nighttime use only and is perfectly fine for daytime. Many say it helps them get through a busy day with minimal distractions.

The smell of Strawberry Diesel is sensational because it inherited a thick but sweet aroma from both parent strains. Many users like it for the scent alone. However, the effects it has are certainly worth noting.
Growing:
Strawberry Diesel is a well-developed and balanced hybrid composed of 50% Cannabis indica and 50% Cannabis sativa. This plant typically has green leaves, though some may turn pink, and the buds may have a pinkish color too. The height of the plant tends to be shorter, which is common with indica strains. This strain does not appear to grow too bushy and is more like a sativa plant.
Strawberry Diesel can be grown indoors or outdoors, and many people prefer to grow this plant inside a greenhouse to contain the pungent smell. Strawberry Diesel is resistant to pests and mold, and caring for this strain regularly will boost the output.
Growing Strawberry Diesel typically results in a yield of 12-14 ounces per square meter yield. This amount is relatively low compared to other cannabis varieties; however, its high THC content makes up for this.

Height

The height is variable. This strain could grow anywhere between 2 and 4 feet tall.

Humidity and Temperature

As with most cannabis varieties, Strawberry Diesel thrives when humidity levels are between 50% to 70% during the vegetative stage. However, reduce the humidity slightly as it progresses into the flowering phase.
The best temperatures for this plant are between 70 and 85 degrees Fahrenheit (21 to 29 degrees Celsius). It must stay indoors if you grow this plant in a cooler area, and grow lamps are an excellent method of maintaining consistent heat.

Flowering

Flowering time usually lasts nine to 10 weeks.

Name: Strawberry Cough
Description:
Strawberry Cough is a sativa-dominant hybrid created by Kyle Kushman that won Best Flower in the 2013 Cannabis Cup. It’s made by crossing Strawberry Fields and an unknown Haze. It is 80% Cannabis sativa and 20% Cannabis indica and has a high THC content, regularly measuring between 20% and 25% THC.

Kushman is credited with creating Joey’s Strain and Cherry Lopez and cultivating Purple Kush, but Strawberry Cough is one of his favorite flavors.

Strawberry Cough is a highly-regarded sativa strain noted for its cerebral, energetic, uplifting effects and sweet, fresh strawberry taste. Due to its effects, Strawberry Cough may be useful for alleviating stress, anxiety, and depression.

Kushman developed Strawberry Cough in California, but one of its parents, Strawberry Fields, is actually an indica from New York. According to legend, this indica was grown next to strawberry fields to mask the odor and started to take on the smell of the strawberries nearby.
Growing:
As Strawberry Cough is a sativa, expect it to grow rather tall. Those living in hot and tropical climates can grow it outdoors, but those in more temperate climates should opt for a greenhouse for optimal growth of this variety of cannabis. As it is resistant to pests and mold, it is a tolerant cultivar to grow for a sativa. Strawberry Cough is an excellent choice for novice gardeners who want to grow cannabis in a greenhouse and blend the best outdoor and indoor growing.

Strawberry Cough can do well indoors, but its height can prove a problem for some. During the vegetative stage, pruning and topping (cutting off the main stalk of a weed plant to force it to grow bushier) may be necessary to control its growth indoors. Strawberry Cough flourishes best when grown in soil and fed organic nutrients. Expect a yield of around 14 to 15 ounces per square meter.

Height

Strawberry Cough can grow up to 78 inches, or 6.5 feet.

Humidity and Temperature

As with most varieties of cannabis, Strawberry Cough does best at a humidity level of around 50% during the vegetative stage, gradually reducing to 30% during the flowering stage. Ideal temperatures are between 70 and 85 degrees Fahrenheit (21 to 29 degrees Celsius) and between 60 and 70 degrees Fahrenheit (15.5 to 21 degrees Celsius) at night.

Flowering

The flowering time is reasonable for a sativa varietal at nine to 10 weeks. Some plants can take 12, 14, or even 16 weeks to flower.

Name: Stardawg
Description:
The Stardawg strain is a pungent sativa-dominant hybrid composed of 60% Cannabis sativa and 40% Cannabis indica. It has moderate to high THC levels, around 22%, and contains no CBD. This strain is known for its offensive aroma and energetic effects.  Stardawg is ideal for managing stress, inflammation, chronic pain, and depression when appropriately dosed.

The Stardawg strain (cultivar) is the love child of parents Chemdawg 4 and Tres Dawg — two well-known hybrid strains from the Top Dawg seed company in the Bay Area of California. Stardawg has a very pungent, earthy scent with strong diesel, chemical, and earthy notes inherited from both parent strains.

This confronting smell can scare some people away, especially beginners or those used to sweet strains. But for cannabis lovers, this strong funky aroma — which has been compared to morning breath and roadkill — adds to the strain’s effects.

As this strain is sativa-dominant, its main effects are energizing and uplifting. It is often used to boost mood and provide clarity. This strain is also well known for its long-lasting high. Stardawg’s effects can last over three hours, longer than most marijuana strains.

For these reasons, Stardawg is a good strain to start your day. Though it comes with a word of caution: this strain’s pungent aroma makes it very hard to be discreet. You might want to keep this in mind if you want to try it before work or in a public setting.

The name Stardawg was coined partly because of its lineage and the star-like trichomes covering the buds’ surface. These crystal-like trichomes are said to be so densely packed on this strain that the buds twinkle like stars in the night sky: A fitting name for a strain that lifts you up and has you swimming in the stars.
Growing:
Stardawg can be grown indoors, outdoors, or in a greenhouse. It is not difficult to grow for an experienced cultivator, but it’s no walk in the park. For that reason, it is not recommended for novice gardeners.

This plant is quite labor-intensive — one of the aspects that makes it better suited to experienced growers — as it requires topping and pruning. Stardawg needs to be topped because it grows upright and is not naturally bushy. Topping the plant makes it bushier, allowing sunlight to hit a larger surface area of the plant, which improves the yield.

When grown indoors, Stardawg can yield 3 ounces per square meter. In an outdoor environment, Stardawg can yield 7 ounces per plant. This yield is not as high as some other cannabis varieties, but many growers think this strain and its potent effects are worth the time and effort.

It is well known that Stardawg products are pungent, and the plant is no exception. You will need to consider the smell if you choose to grow your Stardawg indoors, and many growers use ventilation or air filtration systems to dissipate the smell.

Height

Expect your Stardawg plant to grow up to 47 inches tall.

Humidity and Temperature

Stardawg will thrive in a warm, humid climate like its birthplace in California.

Flowering

If you are growing your Stardawg indoors, it will flower in eight to nine weeks. If you have grown your plant outdoors, it should be ready to harvest in early to mid-October.

Name: Space Queen
Description:
Space Queen is a balanced hybrid strain created by famed breeder Vic High of the British Columbia Growers Association. It crosses Cinderella 99 and Romulan strains (cultivars), with THC levels of 16%-18%. It is 50% sativa and 50% indica, giving it myriad effects.

Space Queen is known for its intense cerebral effects, which give users a boost of energy that eventually mellows into a stressless state. In general, Space Queen is ideal for daytime use and may be useful for managing stress, anxiety, depression, chronic pain, and fatigue.

Space Queen has a deliciously sweet and fruity aroma with berries, vanilla, and cinnamon notes. The taste is equally delicious, with a sweet and citrusy kick.
Growing:
Space Queen produces long, light green buds with bright orange pistils and a dense layer of trichomes.

This plant can be difficult to grow as its height can make it challenging to manage. Intense stretching is common during week three of flowering, and branches need to be supported by a trellis.

Space Queen benefits from “screen of green” (SCROG) training, and it may be necessary to train plants this way if the indoor setup is small. The SCROG method involves topping the plants in the early vegetative stage (removing the apical or center stem).

This encourages the plant to produce more side shoots, eventually becoming colas (flowers). Once topped, the branches of the plants are gently weaved through support (usually a horizontal trellis) to maximize the amount of light reaching each potential bud site.

This plant may need topping multiple times in the vegetative period to keep on top of its height. Tall plants can become weak if they are not tended to carefully. Additives such as silica will help to strengthen plant stems and provide support for large colas.

Space Queen is known to yield 400 grams per square meter indoors and 550 grams per square meter outdoors.

Height

Space Queen will reach 60-80 inches indoors and outdoors.

Humidity and Temperature

Space Queen prefers a warm, arid climate. When growing indoors, keep the relative humidity between 40%-60% in the vegetative phase and drop it to 30%-40% during flowering to prevent molds such as bud rot from taking hold. Space Queen can tolerate warmer temperatures than other strains, and this plant can be grown between 85 and 90 F (26 and 32 C). The humidity may fluctuate with changes in temperature as the air cools and water condenses from it, so continual humidity monitoring is important.

This plant does well in arid environments, but it needs to be given adequate water. When humidity is low, and temperature is high, plants will increase their transpiration rates and suck up more moisture from the soil.

Flowering

The flowering period for this strain is between 50-60 days, making it shorter than many strains.

Name: Sour Diesel
Description:
A sativa-dominant strain, Sour Diesel packs a punch. A motivator and morning kick-start, Sour Diesel is the sworn-by secret weapon of many highly productive people.

For a full wave of energized happiness, the 90% sativa Sour Diesel can help stimulate ideas and set you up to seize the day. This hybrid’s 10% indica content adds depth to the high, helping calm the mind.

While most of Sour Diesel’s effects are helpful, motivating, and positive, some users report feelings of paranoia. SD can over-activate the mind and cause paranoia, stimulating cerebral activity and producing attention difficulties among users.

It is best to enjoy this potent strain among trusted friends to ensure any odd behaviors can be managed. This is not a strain for beginner cannabis users.
Growing:
Sour Diesel is a relatively tricky strain to grow and not a good strain to start with as a beginner grower.
Usually, Sour diesel yields over 10 pounds per plant when grown in the recommended 300-gallon planters. To avoid undeveloped, airy buds, ensure you do not overfeed this plant. On the other hand, keep an eye on nutrient deficiencies, like calcium and nitrogen.
Sour Diesel is often a tall plant, so it is crucial to ensure enough light penetrates the dense canopy while also keeping an eye on the buds. They mustn’t grow too close to the light source if they are grown indoors.

Height

Sour Diesel usually grows tall but does not assume the well-known sativa Christmas tree shape. This plant can reach 10 feet in height.

Humidity and Temperature

Sour Diesel enjoys less than 60% humidity to avoid mold and mildew problems. It also enjoys temperatures below 78 degrees Fahrenheit during the final weeks of flowering to retain the monoterpenes that make Sour Diesel’s aroma so famous.
Make sure to keep up the watering for this thirsty plant.

Flowering

It can take up to 11 weeks for Sour Diesel to bloom. Sour Diesel tends to flower after 70 days in bloom, though it can also be left 80 days in bloom.

Name: Sour Chem
Description:
Sour Chem, also known as Sour Chemdog, is a sativa-dominant hybrid strain that is a cross between Sour Diesel and Chemdog. This strain is known for its high THC content, often reaching up to 26%. Sour Chem is 70% sativa and 30% indica.

Sour Chem is known for its uplifting and energizing effects, making it a popular choice for daytime use. However, due to its high THC content, it should be used with caution by novices. Sour Chem may be beneficial for those dealing with stress, depression, and fatigue. The flavor profile of Sour Chem is often described as sour, diesel-like, and earthy with a hint of citrus.
Growing:
Growing the sour chem strain can be a rewarding experience for both beginners and expert growers. The plant flourishes in both indoor and outdoor environments.

Height

The Sour Chem strain grows to a medium height, and with proper care and attention, growers can expect a high yield.

Humidity and Temperature

Sour chem strain thrives in a controlled environment with temperatures between 70-85°F (21-29°C). The strain prefers a humidity level of around 50% during the vegetative stage, which should be reduced during the flowering stage.

Flowering

The Sour Chem strain typically takes about 9-10 weeks for flowering.

Name: Sour Apple
Description:
Sour Apple is an indica-dominant hybrid bred by Top Shelf Seeds by crossing Cinderella 99 and Sour Diesel. It is an 80% indica and 20% sativa strain (cultivar) with an average THC content of 22%.

Sour Apple combines the best of both indica and sativa varieties. The high begins as a euphoric cerebral experience that uplifts the mood, and this slowly mellows into a relaxing “couch-lock” state typical of indica varieties. This strain may be useful for alleviating stress and insomnia, among other things.

As the name suggests, Sour Apple is a zingy strain with an aroma similar to apple pie. The diesel notes from its parent strains also shine through, giving it a distinct sour apple aroma. Sour Apple also has a delicious intense taste that’s both skunky and sweet.
Growing:
Sour Apple produces fluffy, bright green, and conical buds sprinkled with orange pistils. The buds are dense.

It is a relatively easy strain to grow, but it does get quite large. It is advisable to have a good trimming routine in place to keep this plant healthy and stay on top of vigorous side stems. This plant will also need topping if growing indoors to prevent it from stretching too close to overhead lighting.

Sour Apple may benefit from training techniques such as “screen of green” (SCROG). The SCROG method is performed by topping the plants in the early vegetative stage (removing the apical or center stem).

This encourages the plant to produce more side shoots, eventually becoming colas (flowers). Once topped, the branches of the plants are gently weaved through support (usually a horizontal trellis) to maximize the amount of light reaching each potential bud site.

This plant will typically yield 700 grams per plant outdoors and 500 grams per plant indoors.

Height

Sour Apple can get very tall, especially outdoors, with some growers claiming heights of over 13 feet. Indoors, this plant is expected to reach approximately 60 inches.

Humidity and Temperature

When growing indoors, keep the relative humidity between 40%-60% in the vegetative phase and drop it to 30%-40% during flowering to prevent molds such as bud rot from taking hold. Temperatures should stay between 70-80 F (21-26 C). The humidity may fluctuate with changes in temperature as the water cools and condenses from the air, so continual humidity monitoring is essential.

Flowering

Sour Apple takes a little while to finish flowering; it is usually ready to harvest after nine to 11 weeks.

Name: Snowman
Description:
Snowman is a sativa-dominant strain (cultivar) of cannabis with high THC levels between 23 and 27% and minimal levels of CBD. It was developed from the classic GSC (GSC) strain and is generally 70% sativa and 30% indica. It has been reported to produce long-lasting euphoric, uplifting effects and relieve stress and anxiety.

Snowman is a newer hybrid strain, so little information is available about it compared to older strains. However, many of its properties are similar to those of GSC. To complicate matters, two variations of Snowman exist, one developed by Berners and one by Emerald Family farms. It’s unknown which variation was created.

Snowman was named for its frosty appearance due to its large number of trichomes, which make the plant look like it’s covered in snow. It also possesses burnt orange pistils.

Snowman has a sweet vanilla and diesel aroma that some have described as “gassy kush.” Luckily it tastes a lot sweeter than it smells, with users reporting fruity flavors like apple, citrus, and apricot, as well as nutmeg, spicy herb, and lingering vanilla.
Growing:
Snowman grows similarly to its parent strain Girl Scout Cookies. It can be grown indoors or outdoors, and indoor yields average 1-2 ounces per square foot, and outdoor yields average 18 ounces per plant.

Due to its large, dense buds, Snowman needs regular pruning. This increases airflow and light through the leaves and reduces the risk of mold and mildew developing.

Finding seed stock or clones of Berner’s Snowman can be difficult as not many seed banks or nurseries have it in stock. Other strains may sometimes be mislabeled as Snowman, especially when ordering from a less reputable source.

Height

Because Snowman is a new strain, it hasn’t been observed or reported on enough to know its average height.

Humidity and Temperature

Snowman takes seven to 10 weeks to finish flowering.

Flowering

Snowman prefers warm, humid climates if grown outside.

Name: Skywalker
Description:
A hybrid of Mazar and Blueberry strains, the Skywalker strain is a clean 50/50 split of Cannabis indica and Cannabis sativa. It has a THC level of around 15% and contains almost no CBD. Though this sweet strain (cultivar) is perfectly balanced, it is considered indica-dominant because of its powerful mellowing effect. This makes Skywalker great for managing chronic pain and insomnia.

Skywalker was created in Amsterdam by the seed company Dutch Passion.  The blend of the two indica-dominant hybrid parent strains resulted in the fruity-yet-spicy Skywalker strain. It has a strong blueberry and fruity aroma and flavor with fruity notes and hints of spice and sage.

There is a collection of marijuana strains with a Star Wars namesake, but Skywalker is not named after the heroic Luke Skywalker for the reasons you would think. The urban legend goes that one of the lead cultivators involved in creating the strain was named Luke, and it stuck from there.

The Skywalker strain is the predecessor to the well-known Skywalker Kush/Skywalker OG Kush/Skywalker OG strain. The two often get confused, but Skywalker OG is a potent indica strain — containing 85% indica and 26% THC — which blends the relaxing effects of Skywalker with the high THC content of OG Kush.
Growing:
This plant is reportedly straightforward to grow and is resistant to mold and disease, making it a great option if you are a beginner. It grows better indoors but can be grown outdoors in the right conditions. If you choose to grow your Skywalker outside, it will need to be in hot conditions with temperatures between 68 and 80 degrees Fahrenheit and lots of sunlight.

You can use either Skywalker seeds or clones (cuttings from a mature female plant). The growing process is faster using a clone rather than seeds, but clones can be hard to find and need to be of high quality. With lower-quality clones, there is a risk that any bad traits from the mother plant will be passed down to the clones.

A successful Skywalker plant grown indoors can produce 14 ounces per square meter. An indoor setup will require the temperature to be controlled between 68 and 80 degrees Fahrenheit; sunlight, humidity, and ventilation will also need to be controlled.

Using a hydroponic setup could increase yield by up to 20%. You should only choose a hydroponic setup if you are an experienced grower, as they require more equipment and knowledge.

Height

As this plant is indica-dominant, it won’t reach record-breaking heights and will stay short and bushy, ranging from 30-70 inches in height.

Humidity and Temperature

Skywalker thrives in a hot, dry, and sunny outdoor environment — akin to a Mediterranean climate. When growing indoors, you must replicate this sunny, dry environment. Humidity should be between 65% and 70% during the seedling phase and drop by approximately 5% each week until the flowering stage, and humidity should be no more than 50% by the blooming phase.

Flowering

Skywalker plants grown indoors will flower between eight and nine weeks. If grown outdoors, buds will be ready to harvest by mid to late October.

Name: Skunk
Description:
The Skunk strain of cannabis (sometimes referred to as Super Skunk) is 60% sativa and 40% indica, meaning it is a slightly more sativa-dominant strain (cultivar) with average THC levels ranging between 16 and 20%.

Sensi Seeds created the Skunk strain by combining the Afghani and Skunk #1 strains of cannabis. When creating new strains, Skunk #1 is used often due to its popularity among growers due to its reliability and uniformity, as well as the wide range of phenotypes it can produce.

The Afghani strain originated in the Middle East and was brought to the United States in the 1970s. Both strains are indica-dominant and are known to give the consumer a deep body high without affecting their concentration. Some consumers even report feeling energetic after smoking the Skunk strain, further testament to this variety’s wide range of possible chemical combinations and compositions.

When smoked, the Skunk strain will produce a deeply aromatic and pungent cannabis aroma that many consumers love. When the strain is inhaled, it has a very sweet and fruity flavor profile that surprises many people.
Growing:
The Skunk strain is considered easy to grow, so if you’re just starting your cannabis growing journey, it’s a great strain to get started with. The strain grows well outside in moderate conditions and is known to be resilient to common molds and pests.

However, when growing Skunk strain outside, you need to consider that the strain is very pungent and can attract the attention of neighbors and other people passing by your garden. For this reason, most people prefer to grow it indoors where the climate can be controlled, and extractor fans are used to remove the smell.

Like other sativa-dominant cannabis plants, you can expect your Skunk strain plants to grow to a medium height and yield about 18 ounces per square meter when grown indoors and 20 ounces per plant outdoors.

Height

Skunk strain plants grow to a medium size compared to many other cannabis strains, which means they grow about 4 to 8 feet tall. During the growing process, they require very little maintenance, whether grown indoors or outside in your garden.

Humidity and Temperature

The Skunk strain thrives in a moderate climate and is very resilient when grown outdoors. However, most people prefer to grow the strain indoors due to the strong, pungent smell that the plants emit. They can control the temperature and humidity and remove the smell using extractor fans.

Flowering

You can expect a flowering time of eight to 10 weeks when grown indoors. To maximize your yield of Skunk strain buds, you can wait closer to 10 weeks before harvesting your plants. When grown outdoors, it will typically start to flower in late September or early October.

Description:
An indica-dominant hybrid cross between DJ Short Blueberry and an unknown Afghani strain, Shishkaberry has remained top-of-mind among cannabis consumers since its second-place finish at the 2001 High Times Cannabis Cup. The Shishkaberry strain’s most ardent fans laud its high THC levels of up to 26% for providing relaxing effects that help alleviate chronic pain.

Although it’s not named after an actual berry, Shishkaberry’s sweet, berry-like aroma with slightly earthy notes would convince you that it was. Its parent strains gifted it with covetable genetics; Shishkaberry’s buds tend to be dense and flower within eight to 10 weeks. Its resilience makes it an excellent strain (cultivar) for novice cultivators to grow.

Experienced marijuana consumers and novice users claim that Shishkaberry is one of the best indica-dominant hybrid strains for people seeking deep relaxation that envelops the entire body. As one might expect from a strain with 80% indica genetics, Shishkaberry can also bring about powerful sedative effects.
Growing:
Shishkaberry is an easy strain for expert and novice cultivators to embrace. In its eight to 10 week harvesting time, Shishkaberry can produce up to 16 ounces of bud per square meter indoors. If grown outdoors, its ideal harvesting month is October.

Height

Shishkaberry reportedly grows between six to seven feet tall.

Humidity and Temperature

Shishkaberry can be successfully grown indoors, outdoors, or in a greenhouse. Ideal indoor temperatures range between 70 and 80 degrees Fahrenheit, and if grown outdoors, this indica-dominant hybrid thrives in temperate, sunny climates. Relative humidity of around 50-60% is ideal during the vegetative phase and approximately 40% during the flowering phase.

Flowering

Shishkaberry’s flowering time is typically between eight and 10 weeks.

Name: Shark Shock
Description:
Shark Shock, also known as Great White Shark and Peacemaker, is an indica-dominant strain of cannabis with THC levels between 12% and 21%. Shantibaba developed the strain (cultivar) while working at Greenhouse Seeds in the 1990s by crossing parent plants White Widow with Skunk #1. Shark Shock may be useful for managing chronic pain, nausea, stress, anxiety, and depression.

The strain is approximately 80% indica and 20% sativa and has been reported as producing rapid and intense cerebral highs that sometimes turn euphoric, followed by physical relaxation. The scent has been described as sweet, skunky, and citrus-like, and a fruity taste with sweet, skunky, pungent, earthy, fruity, and citrus-like flavors.

Some users also describe it as garlicky. Shark Shock has won numerous awards, including the High Times Cannabis Cup (Bio) award in 1997.
Growing:
Shark Shock has been reported to flower in seven weeks when grown indoors, with a yield of around 17-21 ounces per square meter or approximately 400-600 grams per square meter.

When grown outdoors, it should be ready for harvest between late September and early October, with yields of 16-18 ounces per plant, which is about 450 to 510 grams per plant.

Name: Sensi Star
Description:
Sensi Star is an indica-dominant strain of cannabis developed by Paradise Seeds. First released in 1995, Paradise Seeds released an updated version in 1997, claiming enhanced stability. The exact genetics of the strain (cultivar) has been kept under wraps; however, some estimates have put it at 65% indica and 35% sativa, while other estimates place it as high as 90% indica.

Sensi Star has high THC levels, often around 18%-22%, and has been described as “the strongest indica you will ever encounter.” These days, the THC percentages of Sensi Star have been surpassed, but it is still considered a strong strain useful for managing chronic pain, insomnia, and nausea.

The scent has been described as akin to fresh pine mixed with lemon, and the flavors have been described as earthy, herbal, and pear-like. High levels of oil production make it prized by hash producers.

Since its introduction in 1995 and improvement in 1997 by Paradise Seeds, Sensi Star has won over 15 Cannabis Cup awards. It has also won awards in several other competitions, including La Bella Flor, Champions Cup, Copa Mendoza, and Soft Secrets Plant of the Year.

The popularity of Sensi Star has inspired many cannabis breeders to use it as a parent strain for developing other hybrids. At least 55 strains (cultivars) of cannabis claim Sensi Star as part of their heritage. Some of these strains have become famous in their own right, including Bio-Diesel, Stevie Wonder, Death Star, Lemon Stinky, and Sensitron.
Growing:
Sensi Star can be grown indoors and outdoors, yielding up to 16 ounces of cannabis per plant when grown indoors. It tends to grow short and stout, with bushy branches and dense indica buds, meaning some pruning may be needed. Excess moisture should be avoided as this strain is susceptible to mold and bud rot.

Name: Romulan
Description:
Romulan is an indica-dominant cannabis strain with sedating, tranquilizing and narcotic-like effects. Reports suggest that Romulan could help manage chronic pain, insomnia, and appetite loss. Its candy, earthy, pine, and citrus flavors create a refreshing overall experience.

These days, Romulan contains 75% Cannabis indica and 25% Cannabis sativa genetics. However, it was initially believed to be a 100% pure indica strain. Romulan’s parent strains aren’t entirely known, but White Rhino (an indica strain) is one, and the other is likely to be a type of North American indica cannabis strain.

Next Generation Seeds initially produced Romulan, and it’s thought that a breeder called Romulan Joe was influential in creating this strain.

In terms of its appearance, Romulan produces dense and frosty buds. It has brightly colored brassy-orange pistils that can be found between the bright green sugar leaves, with frosty buds that are packed tightly together.

Romulan gets its name from the fictional Star Trek alien species with ridges on their forehead and pointed ears. People have joked that when using Romulan, you could “dent your head” because it is so strong.

The Romulan strain is well-known and mentioned in Skunk, High Times, and Cannabis Culture. It also won third place for Best Non-Solvent Hash in the 2017 High Times Medical Cannabis Cup.
Growing:
Romulan can be grown indoors and outdoors, and it’s relatively easy to grow and manageable for novice users.

Romulan is resistant to many diseases, insects and mold. Because of this, it doesn’t require as much maintenance as some other strains do.

The Romulan strain has a similar yield when grown indoors and outdoors. You can expect a yield of about 9 ounces (255 grams) of bud per square meter.

Romulan is a stocky plant that grows many branches. This means that the “Sea of Green” (SoG) method (growing many small cannabis plants in a limited space) and the “Screen of Green” method (growing cannabis plants through a horizontal screen) are both suited for the Romulan strain.

Height

Although the Romulan strain is relatively short, it often grows taller than other indica-dominant strains. It’s essential to ensure that it has enough space to branch up and grow upwards.
You can expect Romulan to reach heights from 60 to 80 inches (approximately 1.5 to 2 meters).

Humidity and Temperature

Romulan plants grow best in a sunny, warm, and dry environment. A Mediterranean-like climate is described as being optimal for growing Romulan.
Temperatures between 68 and 78 degrees Fahrenheit (20 and 26 degrees Celsius) are suitable for growing Romulan.

Flowering

The average flowering time for a Romulan plant is eight to nine weeks. If you grow Romulan outdoors, you can expect it to be ready to harvest in mid-October (in the Northern Hemisphere).
