Name: Purple Urkle
Description:
A strain of disputed parentage, Purple Urkle is an indica-dominant hybrid composed of 80% Cannabis indica and 20% Cannabis sativa. It has THC levels of around 20% but has been measured as high as 26%. This strain has relaxing, sedative effects, putting many people to sleep. Purple Urkle could therefore help manage chronic pain and insomnia.

The origins of Purple Urkle — sometimes called Purple Urple — are a mystery. It is thought that this strain is a phenotype of either Mendocino Purps or Granddaddy Purple that emerged from the Emerald Triangle in Northern California in the ‘80s. Either way, Purple Urkle has many similarities to other cultivars in the Purple Family, including an indica-dominant genotype, relaxing effects, fruity grape flavors, and velvety undertones.

Purple Urkle is named after Steve Urkle, the main character of the television show “Family Matters.” Jaleel White, the actor who plays the legendary Steve Urkle on the show, announced in 2021 that he was joining the cannabis industry. In partnership with 710 Labs, Jaleel is launching a line of Purple Urkle variants called “ItsPurpl.”

Purple Urkle weed is popular among cannabis users for its sweet, fruity taste. This strain has strong grape notes — often described as tasting like grape soda — with some earthy undertones. Some people also pick up notes of berries and plums. The grape theme is continued in Purple Urkle’s appearance. The calyxes of the flowers are a velvety purple color.

Purple Urkle produces an indica-dominant full-body high that relaxes you from head to toe. This calming blend is used to calm the mind, help you sleep, relieve aches and pains, or just sit back and relax when you want to. Because of this, Purple Urkle is a nighttime strain.
Growing:
Purple Urkle plants can be tricky to grow, especially from seeds. Experts agree that you will need some growing experience to be able to tackle this strain and that it’s much easier to grow it from a clone or cutting. Purple Urkle also requires attention to its nutrient supply and is susceptible to mold and disease, adding further complexity.

This strain can be grown indoors and outdoors, though it’s unique in that indoor plants yield more than those grown outdoors. Successful indoor plants can yield around 18 ounces per 10 square feet, whereas outdoor plants won’t yield more than 9 ounces per plant. This, combined with shorter flowering periods, makes indoor growing more economical. Experienced growers may consider using a hydroponic setup or the “Sea of Green” (SoG) method to increase yield further.

Height

Expect this plant to stay short and bushy, like a typical indica plant. It will reach between 40 to 55 inches tall.

Humidity and Temperature

Outdoor plants will need a hot, sunny climate like the Emerald Triangle in Northern California, with temperatures between 72 and 80 degrees Fahrenheit. For indoor growing, you will need to control the temperature and humidity, and seedlings and clones will need high humidity of around 75%-80%.
This drops gradually when the plant enters the vegetative state and should be below 50% by the flowering stage. If you choose to grow your Purple Urkle indoors, you will have to ensure that you have good airflow to avoid mold and disease — a good indication that the conditions are not right is if the plants start to smell unpleasant.

Flowering

Expect indoor plants to flower in eight to nine weeks. Expect outdoor plants to be ready for harvest by mid-October.

Purple Mr. Nice Guy, also known as Purple Nice Guy, is an indica-dominant hybrid strain that is a cross between the legendary G13 strain and the Hash Plant. Some enthusiasts argue that it is a cross between Granddaddy Purple and Mr. Nice. Purple Mr. Nice Guy is known for its high THC content, which averages around 22% but can reach up to 24%. This strain is composed of 70% indica and 30% sativa.

Purple Mr. Nice Guy is renowned for its calming and soothing effects, making it a favorite among those seeking relief from stress and anxiety. However, beginners should approach this strain with caution due to its potent psychoactive effects. The high THC content of Purple Mr. Nice Guy may also make it beneficial for those dealing with chronic pain, insomnia, and lack of appetite. This strain is characterized by its unique flavor profile, which combines sweet, spicy, and earthy notes with a hint of grape and berry.
Growing:
The Purple Mr. Nice Guy strain is a versatile hash plant that adapts well to both indoor and outdoor growing conditions. It’s an excellent strain for those with moderate growing experience.

Height

Plants of this strain usually grow to a medium height and can yield up to 500 grams per square meter indoors, and up to 600 grams per plant if grown outdoors.

Humidity and Temperature

This strain prefers cooler climates with temperatures ranging from 20-30°C. A relative humidity of 40-50% is ideal.

Flowering

The flowering time for Purple Mr Nice Guy plants is approximately 8-9 weeks.

Name: Purple Kush
Description:
Purple Kush is a classic pure indica cannabis strain reminiscent of the Hindu Kush mountains in Afghanistan. Due to its powerful and relaxing effects on the body, combined with its earthy aroma and bright purple color, Purple Kush has become increasingly popular over the years.

It’s a cross between the Hindu Kush and the Afghani Purple strains and is described as a descendant of the original Kush landrace strain. It is a “pure indica,” as it is 100% indica with no sativa influence.

It’s thought that Purple Kush was created in the 1960s or 1970s. Initially, it was bred in Oakland, California. However, Purple Kush has genetic connections to the Hindu Kush mountains between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

The popularity of the Purple Kush strain earned it a place in High Times magazine’s Top 10 marijuana strains in 2016.

Purple Kush cannabis has a subtle, earthy, and spicy aroma. It has strong yet sweet flavors, which may remind you of berries and grapes.

It produces average-sized flowers containing tightly packed buds. In addition, Purple Kush has sticky resin, a common characteristic of other Afghan cannabis strains.
Growing:
Purple Kush can be grown indoors or outdoors. However, it may be easier to grow Purple Kush indoors so that you can control the environment to ensure optimal growing conditions.
If you grow Purple Kush outdoors, ensure the area has lots of sunlight. Since Purple Kush grows relatively low to the ground, it can be more challenging for the sun to reach the low-lying leaves.
Purple Kush grows best in soil, but a hydroponics system can also be used as long as the humidity is kept to a minimum.
Purple Kush is resistant to mold and some pests, making it easier to grow.
Purple Kush generally produces around 14 ounces of bud per square meter. However, it only has about 8 ounces of bud per square meter if grown outdoors.

Height

Since Purple Kush is a pure indica strain, it doesn’t grow as tall as other strains, and you can expect it to grow to three feet (91.4 cm). Rather than growing tall, Purple Kush grows bushy and wide.

Humidity and Temperature

The environment should be dry to grow Purple Kush because rain and humidity can cause the buds to rot.
Purple Kush grows well in cool to moderate temperatures as a cold climate is perfect for allowing the bright purple color to develop. A temperature between 65 and 75 degrees Fahrenheit (18 and 24 degrees Celsius) is thought to be optimal.

Flowering

Purple Kush flowers relatively quickly, usually at around eight weeks.
If it’s grown outdoors, Purple Kush is usually ready to be harvested in mid- to late-September in the Northern Hemisphere.

Name: Purple Haze
Description:
The Purple Haze strain of cannabis was made famous by the classic 1967 Jimi Hendrix song of the same name. It also contains small speaks of purple flower that helped to give it the Purple Haze name. At 60% sativa and 40% indica, Purple Haze is a sativa-dominant hybrid that is the love child of the Purple Thai and Haze strains.

With a typical THC content of between 14% to 19%, you can expect to feel a deep sense of euphoria that will unleash your creative side and leave you feeling a sense of contentment for long periods.

When smoked, Purple Haze gives off a dreamy mix of sweet and earthy flavors like berry, lavender, and grape that transport even the most veteran smokers back to their glory days of going on psychedelic adventures.

Purple Haze is a cross between the two sativa-dominant parent strains of Purple Thai and Haze. Both strains in the Purple Haze lineage originated in Thailand, but they and the hybrid Purple Haze are now growing worldwide.

Most people believe the strain is named after the Jimi Hendrix song Purple Haze while others think the song was named after the strain containing small speaks of a purple flower. Either way, the strain is very much linked to Hendrix and the 1960s. Purple Haze became an instant favorite due to its euphoric effects that help people become more creative.
Growing:
Purple Haze is considered an easy strain to grow, and it can be grown successfully in indoor and outdoor environments and particularly likes a warm and sunny climate. If you have a garden with plenty of sunshine and high-quality soil, you should get an excellent yield from Purple Haze plants.

Like other sativa-dominant cannabis plants, you can expect your Purple Haze to grow to a medium height and yield 19 ounces per square meter when grown indoors and 14 ounces per plant outdoors. The only downside of Purple Haze is that the plants require some maintenance, but the high yield makes it worth it.

Height

Purple Haze strain plants grow to a medium size compared to other strains. Expect them to reach between 4and 8feet tall. During the growing process, they will require some regular maintenance to ensure you maximize your yield.

Humidity and Temperature

When grown outdoors, purple Haze thrives in a warm, sunny, Mediterranean-type climate. Alternatively, it makes a great strain to grow hydroponically. Purple Haze plants need to be planted in good quality soil and love the sun, and they can survive well in direct sunlight for long periods of the day without any trouble.

Flowering

When grown indoors, you can expect a flowering time of seven to nine weeks. To maximize your yield of Purple Haze buds, you can wait longer before harvesting your plants. When grown outdoors, it will typically start to flower in late October each year.

Purple Afghani is a hardy strain, suited for both indoor and outdoor growth. Its compact size is perfect for limited indoor spaces, and it thrives outdoors in a Mediterranean climate.

Purple Afghani usually grows to an average height, producing a moderate to high yield depending on growing conditions and care given.

Purple Afghan enjoys somewhat dry and mild temperature climates. Maintaining a temperature of about 70°F and low humidity in the flowering stage is critical to prevent mold formation.

Flowering

Pure Power Plant has a short flowering time of around 8-10 weeks for indoor growing.

Description:

The moderate THC content of Pure Love may make it beneficial for those dealing with chronic pain, insomnia, and lack of appetite. Pure Love is often described as having a sweet, floral, earthy, and slightly spicy flavor profile.

Pure Love is a giant plant offering an above-average yield, making it a favorite among growers. It fares well both indoors and outdoors and is recommended for intermediate to experienced growers due to its specific needs for optimal growth.

Height

Pure Love plants can grow up to 80 inches tall, yielding approximately 18 ounces per plant when grown outdoors and slightly less indoors, around 16 ounces per square meter.

Pure Love prefers a warm and humid climate, similar to Mediterranean environments. Maintaining temperatures about 70-80 degrees Fahrenheit and a humidity level of 40-50% is crucial for optimal growth.

Name: Pure Kush
Description:
Pure Kush, also known as OG Kush, is a potent indica-dominant strain with a strong genetic backbone. It is believed to be a cross between Chemdawg and Hindu Kush. Pure Kush is renowned for its high THC content, which averages around 24%, but can sometimes reach up to 27%. The strain is composed of 75% indica and 25% sativa, making it a favorite among those seeking a heavy, relaxing high.

Pure Kush is known for its deeply calming and sedative effects, making it a popular choice for those dealing with stress, anxiety, and insomnia. However, due to its high THC content, it is recommended that beginners approach this strain with caution. Pure Kush’s potential therapeutic benefits may also include relief from chronic pain and stimulation of appetite. Growing:
Pure Kush is suitable for both indoor and outdoor cultivation. The plant is incredibly hardy and resilient and can survive harsh outdoor circumstances. With a flowering time of about 9 weeks, it offers a decent yield for growers. It has a clone-only strain, so growers should obtain a healthy clone from a reputable source.

Height

Pure Kush plants generally grow medium in height, making them ideal for indoor cultivation. With proper care, growers can expect moderate to high yields from each plant.

Humidity and Temperature

Pure Kush plants thrive in a humid environment with a temperature range of 70-85°F (21-29°C). As the flowering phase begins, the humidity level should be reduced to prevent bud rot.

Flowering

The flowering time for Pure Kush is approximately 8-9 weeks. This relatively swift maturation allows growers to produce an efficient crop rotation.

Description:
Pure Afghan, also known as Afghan Kush, is a pure indica strain originating from the mountainous region of Afghanistan. Height

Pure Afghan prefers dry and warm conditions, similar to its origin in Afghanistan. It will do well in temperatures between 70-85°F and a relative humidity of 30-50%.

Name: Pre-98 Bubba Kush
Description:
Pre-98 Bubba Kush is an indica-dominant strain originating in the ‘90s. The exact heritage of this strain (cultivar) is disputed, but some believe it comes from a landrace strain imported from Pakistan or Afghanistan. It’s an 85% indica and 15% sativa hybrid with average THC levels of 20%.

Pre-98 Bubba Kush is a classic strain loved by many old-school and new-school cannabis connoisseurs. It is a typical indica strain ideal for nighttime use and has sedative and relaxing effects, which can help alleviate symptoms of chronic pain, insomnia and stress.

This strain has an earthy, pungent smell with citrus undertones, and users might notice a delicate coffee flavor on the exhale. It’s an ideal strain to use after a long day and to get users ready for a night of deep relaxation and sleep.
Growing:
This variety produces large green buds with purple hues. The flowers are covered in wispy white pistils sprinkled with an amber frost as it matures. The leaves are large and broad, and growers report luscious growth with compact nodes.

This variety will be suitable for beginner growers as it is relatively easy to grow. It is a compact plant that displays good branching that is easily manageable. Trimming some of the larger fan leaves of this variety will be essential to allow light to enter the lower canopy and improve air circulation.

Pre-98 Bubba Kush is well-suited to a hydroponic system and is a medium feeder. Although it is a compact plant, training it may improve yields and respond well to “screen of green” training. The SCROG method is topping the plants in the early vegetative stage.

This encourages the plant to produce more side shoots, eventually becoming colas (flowers). Once topped, the branches of the plants are gently weaved through support (usually a horizontal trellis) to maximize the amount of light reaching each potential bud site.

This plant is a medium yielder, averaging 300 grams per square meter indoors and 400 grams per square meter outdoors.

Height

Pre-98 Bubba Kush will typically grow from 60 to 80 inches indoors and outdoors.

Humidity and Temperature

This strain prefers a warmer climate outdoors. When growing Pre-98 Bubba Kush, keep the relative humidity between 40%-60% in the vegetative phase, and drop it to 30%-40% during flowering to prevent molds such as bud rot from taking hold. Temperatures should stay in the 71-82 F (22-28 C) range.

Flowering

The flowering period for this variety is slightly longer than typical indica strains at around nine weeks (63 days). However, some growers claim to harvest at approximately seven weeks.

Name: Platinum Kush
Description:
Platinum Kush is a popular hybrid cannabis strain. It’s indica-dominant, containing 90% cannabis indica and 10% cannabis sativa genetics. Although the exact genetic background of Platinum Kush isn’t known, it’s believed to be made by crossing OG Kush and an unknown Afghani strain.

Platinum Kush has a sweet, earthy, hashy, and almost skunky aroma. When the flowers are broken up, however, it often smells tangy. The flavor of Platinum Kush is fruity, sweet, and woody.
Purple hues and bright orange hairs characterize its appearance. However, Platinum Kush gets its name from its different platinum-silver color. A shiny silver coat of crystal resin covers the flowers and leaves.

The Platinum Kush strain, also known as Platinum OG Kush or Platinum OG, was developed by Apothecary Genetics in the early 1990s. Since then, Platinum Kush has become increasingly popular, as demonstrated by its Best Hydro Strain win in the 1994 High Times Cup.

Platinum Kush is commonly grown on the United States West Coast and in Colorado.
Growing:
Platinum Kush is an indica variety of cannabis that is relatively easy to grow and can be successfully grown indoors and outdoors. Autoflower versions of this popular strain/cultivar also exist, making Platinum Kush Auto an ideal choice for those seeking more discreet growth.

It’s also resistant to environmental threats, including fungi, mold, bacteria, and insects.

When Platinum Kush is grown indoors, you can expect a yield of approximately 18 ounces (or around 500 grams) per square meter. However, a yield of about 14 ounces (or 400 grams) per square meter is expected when grown outdoors, and this is slightly less than other cannabis strains.

Platinum Kush is thought to grow exceptionally well using the “Sea of Green” method. This is where you grow many small plants simultaneously in a contained area instead of a few larger plants in an uncrowded area.

Trimming your Platinum Kush cannabis plant as it grows regularly is essential. This is because, being an indica, it can grow quite bushy and wide.

Height

Platinum Kush plants usually grow to medium height, typically between 30 to 50 inches (76 to 127 cm). As an indica-dominant strain, it doesn’t grow as high as sativas tend to.

Humidity and Temperature

Platinum Kush is reported to grow best in an environment that is dry and warm. However, since Platinum Kush is resistant to mold, it can also grow in humid climates.

The optimal temperature for growing Platinum Kush is between 65 to 80 degrees Fahrenheit (18 to 26 degrees Celsius).

Flowering

Platinum Kush flowering time is generally eight to nine weeks. If grown outside, it should be ready to harvest by September or October (in the Northern Hemisphere).

An excellent way to tell that a Platinum Kush plant is ready to harvest is that the buds develop their characteristic platinum-silver sparkle.

Name: Platinum Cookies
Description:
Platinum Cookies, also known as Platinum GSC, PGSC, and Platinum GSC, is an indica-dominant cannabis hybrid (60% indica and 40% sativa) that evolved from the indomitable Cookies strain. Platinum Cookies could help manage chronic pain, anxiety, and depression.

The parent strain was developed in Northern California by a collective called the Cookie Family, whose genetics have come to dominate the West Coast cannabis market. Cookies is the strain (cultivar) that made the collective famous, with Platinum Cookies being the latest in a series of delightful offshoots, including its close cousin Thin Mint Cookies.

PGSC is a hybrid strain that crosses OG Kush, Durban Poison, and a third unknown strain. Platinum Cookies perfectly marry the dreamy, relaxing power of Kush with the creative zest of Durban Poison, making Platinum Cookies a highly sought-after, versatile strain with sweet berries and candy fragrance, along with berry flavors.

With THC levels of 17%-22%, Platinum Cookies is considered relatively potent, with a THC content suitable for those seeking relief from pain and anxiety. Users report heady feelings of relaxation, euphoria, and contentment. Boasting moderate cannabidiol (CBD) levels, Platinum Cookies can also be used as an effective mood enhancer.
Growing:
Platinum Cookies is a versatile strain that can be successful when grown indoors or outdoors. Grown indoors, it will yield around 12 ounces per square meter and is likely to produce relatively small, tight buds covered in trichomes. The “platinum” refers to the intense frosty color of the fully developed buds.

Outdoor growers can expect higher yields of around 16 ounces per plant. However, this is only when the conditions are hot and dry. Experienced growers recommend using a greenhouse if possible, as it offers the hands-off advantages of an outdoor grow but allows better control over the climate.

Height

Platinum Cookies is a tall plant growing between 5 and 6 feet tall.

Humidity and Temperature

This strain thrives at lower humidity levels — between 55%-70% during the growing stage.

Flowering

Platinum Cookies has an average flowering time of eight to nine weeks

Name: Pink Rozay
Description:
Pink Rozay is a strongly indica-dominant hybrid strain with around 80% indica and 20% sativa. It has been reported as having relaxing, sleepy effects and could help manage anxiety, insomnia, and chronic pain.

It’s a product of Lemonchello and Lemon Pound Cake, resulting in a THC level of around 17%. It’s an attractive option for novice users with its distinct fruity scent and moderate THC levels.

Pink Rozay weed was first created by Cookies Farm in San Francisco, combining Lemonchello and London Pound Cake genetics. It was inspired by the vibrant colors you see when drinking a glass of Rose — to help its users get that sophisticated feeling they’ve been looking for.

Like the wine, Pink Rozay provides bright floral flavors but can sometimes leave your mouth a little dry. Nonetheless, it is enjoyed by novices and connoisseurs for its enticing aroma and flavors.
Growing:
Pink Rozay marijuana is easy to grow, making it a great option for beginner growers. It’s versatile to grow indoors and outdoors and responds well to topping to encourage the growth of multiple colas. Defoliation, trimming, and pruning are also essential to thin the canopy of this plant to further aid growth.

Other growers recommend weekly checks for spiders and caterpillars that may impact your yield. Indoor yield sits at around 400-450 grams per square meter, while outdoor 400-450 grams per plant. Buds are available as both autoflowering and photoperiod seeds.

Height

Outdoor height up to 65 inches (170cm)

Humidity and Temperature

Pink Rozay is best grown at a relative humidity (RH) of around 70% initially, then gradually lowered to 40% RH in the flowering stage. Lowering the humidity as you reach the flowering stage is vital to avoid potential mold damaging your crop. This strain has a tight bud structure, making it more prone to trapping moisture and attracting mold.

Flowering

Nine to 10 weeks

Name: Pineapple Express
Description:
Pineapple Express is a sativa-dominant strain of cannabis with a THC content of around 20%. The hybrid cross is made of Trainwreck and Hawaiian strains and is 60% sativa, and 40% indica and has been reported as having energizing, revitalizing effects.

G13 Labs created this strain of cannabis about five years before the film of the same name in 2008 but named it “Pineapple Express” after the film was released. Pineapple Express is said to have a tropical, mango, and pineapple flavor and scent.
Growing:
Pineapple Express is a hybrid cannabis variety that does well indoors and out. It is generally recommended to grow Pineapple Express in soil and, if planting outdoors, to protect it from too much wind to prevent the stalks from snapping. Pineapple Express can produce yields of up to 19 ounces per plant or square meter. Silica sprays or root feeds may also help boost the plant’s strength and yield.

Due to its genetics, you may get a wide variety of Pineapple Express phenotypes, from the more common sativa-dominant, uplifting plants to the shorter, more relaxing indica varieties. This can make Pineapple Express ideal for those who are looking to grow several types of cannabis plants with different effects for different times of the day.

Expect Pineapple Express to grow between 3.5 and 6 feet, depending on the phenotype.

Humidity and Temperature

Pineapple Express enjoys a warm, Mediterranean and maritime climate. It is best to keep your grow room at a temperature of between 68 and 77 degrees Fahrenheit (20 to 25 degrees Celsius) during the day in the vegetative stage, with a humidity level of around 50%. Piña Colada is a hybrid strain that is a cross between Romulan and Island Sweet Skunk. It has a balanced ratio of indica to sativa, making it a versatile strain for both relaxation and stimulation. Piña Colada has a moderate THC content, averaging around 20%.

Name: Peanut Butter Breath
Description:
Peanut Butter Breath, a.k.a. Peanut Butter or Peanut Breath, is an evenly balanced hybrid strain (cultivar) that packs a punch. With a THC content of 26%, you can expect a hard-hitting cerebral high that sends a buzz around your entire body. Its effects suggest that Peanut Butter Breath would be ideal for managing stress & inflammation, anxiety and depression, chronic pain, and insomnia.

Peanut Butter Breath originated from ThugPug Genetics and is a cross between Do-Si-Do and the exceedingly rare Mendo Breath. Balanced strains, i.e., those with 50% indica and 50% sativa, are generally quite hard to come by. As the name implies, Peanut Butter Breath offers a deliciously sweet, buttery, nutty flavor like a candy peanut butter cup.

Peanut Butter Breath won first place in Toronto’s 2019 Karma Cup in the indica category. It’s popular for its pleasantly relaxing effects and delicious smell.
Growing:
A warning if you want to grow this strain: You may need to do some serious investigative work. ThugPug is secretive about this strain, making their seeds challenging to come by. The strain is also more delicate and less resistant to mold than other strains. You may be better off growing it indoors.

Overall, we recommend Peanut Butter Breath for more experienced growers. Indoors, you can expect a yield of around 0.5 ounces per square foot (150 grams per square meter). Outdoors produce approximately 10-12 ounces (280-340 grams).

Buds are generally long, with hints of purple and a heavy coat of trichomes. You should slowly dry and cure buds to preserve and maximize the terpenes.

Height

Peanut Butter Breath strain is a tall plant, and you can boost its vertical growth by providing plenty of room for the roots and maximizing light exposure.

Humidity and Temperature

Peanut Butter Breath grows best in a Mediterranean climate. Humidity for this strain needs to be strictly controlled, given its susceptibility to mold.
During the growing period, humidity should be kept at around 70%. As you near the flowering stage, gradually lower this to 40% to prevent any excess moisture from being trapped.

Flowering time for this strain is relatively typical at nine to 11 weeks. Growing outdoors, you can expect to harvest in late October.

Description:
Panama Red is a classic, pure sativa strain that originated in Panama. This strain has a lower average THC content, typically ranging between 10% and 16%. Panama Red is 100% sativa.

Panama Red is known for its cerebral and energetic effects, making it a popular choice for those seeking creativity and sociability. However, it can also lead to a feeling of paranoia in some users due to its strong cerebral high. Panama Red may be beneficial for managing stress, depression, fatigue, and pain. The strain is said to have a sweet, earthy, and woody flavor profile.
Growing:
Panama Red is better suited for experienced growers, as it requires consistent care and attention due to its long flowering time, strong odor, and vulnerability to pests. This strain is ideal for both indoor and outdoor cultivation. However, it performs better in outdoor environments with warm, humid climates.

Height

The Panama Red strain grows tall, with long, thick stems and thin leaves. Expect a moderate yield of about 1-2 ounces per square foot, depending on the plant’s health and growing conditions.

Humidity and Temperature

The Panama Red cannabis strain thrives in a warm, humid climate, similar to its native environment in Panama. Growers should aim for temperatures between 70-85°F (21-29°C) and maintain a humidity level of around 60-70% during the vegetative stage. As the plants flower, lowering the humidity to 40-50% is recommended to prevent mold and bud rot.

Flowering

Panama Red requires one of the longest flowering periods: 11 to 14 weeks. This long flowering time allows the plant to develop fully and produce resin-rich buds, ideal for a potent sativa experience. *Humidity and Temperature**

The flowering time for the Pai Gow strain is approximately 8 to 10 weeks, allowing the plants ample time to produce potent, high-quality buds.

Name: Oreoz
Description:
Oreoz strain is a potent hybrid marijuana strain from 3rd Coast Genetics that crosses Secret Weapon and Cookies and Cream strains. This indica-dominant hybrid strain is known for its long-lasting effects, great taste, and powerful body buzz.

Name: OG Kush
Description:
OG Kush, also called Premium OG Kush, was created during the early 1990s in Florida. No one is sure how OG Kush was made. However, it’s been suggested in the cannabis industry that the genetics originate from popular strains (cultivars) such as Chemdawg, Lemon Thai, or Old World Paki Kush, which could have been cross-bred to produce this plant.

This plant is renowned for its unique terpene profile, which gives it a strong aroma of lemon. Many say it’s one of the most uplifting cannabis strains available. OG Kush’s effects suggest it helps manage anxiety, depression, and chronic pain. Another top-reported effect is hunger, so OG Kush may benefit appetite loss and cachexia associated with cancer or AIDS/HIV.

OG Kush is an indica-dominant strain. Most plants are 55% indica and 45% sativa, although there could be slight variations with different crossbreeds. This plant has high THC levels of around 26%, and OG Kush also contains some CBD.

This plant is recommended for expert growers because it does not like being confined to a flower pot, instead preferring plenty of space to grow outdoors.
Growing:
OG Kush is an indica-dominant strain. Because of this, it may not grow to the same height as a sativa plant. However, growers say this strain tends to grow quite bushy and prefers plenty of space.

OG Kush can be grown indoors, but it will thrive much better when grown outdoors. Hence, it might not be ideal for first-time growers or those desiring to cultivate cannabis discreetly. When grown outdoors, growers can expect a moderate yield of 17 ounces (480 grams) per plant.

Like most cannabis plants, you do not need to worry too much about pests because OG Kush produces natural compounds that repel most bugs. However, taking good care of this strain is vital because it might be more prone to mold or mildew since it’s a bushy plant. Pruning leaves before the flowering stage will prevent mildew and significantly improve the health of this plant. Adding calcium and magnesium to the soil will also improve health.

Height

OG Kush can grow up to 40 inches or 3.3 feet (1 meter).

Humidity and Temperature

Unlike most cannabis plants, OG Kush thrives well in a slightly lower humidity during the vegetative stage. Keep the humidity around 50% and reduce it to about 30% to 35% during the flowering stage to prevent mold from growing on the buds.

OG Kush can also handle slightly lower temperatures between 65 and 80 degrees Fahrenheit (18-26 degrees Celsius). Because of this, it’s well adjusted to lower temperatures at night.

This strain could be ideal for you if you live in a cooler climate.

Flowering

Eight to nine weeks. Most indicas typically finish flowering in about six to nine weeks.

Name: Northern Lights
Description:
Northern Lights (NL) is 95% indica and 5% sativa, with a THC content between 16% and 21% and relatively little CBD at around 0.1%. NL crosses Afghani and Thai sativa varieties and produces euphoric, sedative, “couch lock” effects. NL is now a classic cannabis strain used in many breeding projects, as it is quite a stable strain with uniform growth patterns.

Many seed banks and breeders have their version of Northern Lights, although the original genetics may be found in packs of seeds by Mr. Nice, Sensi Seeds, and Dr. Atomic Seeds.

The precise origin of Northern Lights is a mystery, although some sources claim it was developed by a breeder known as “The Indian” in Washington during the 1970s. There were 11 different versions of NL, with numbers 1, 2, and 5 becoming the most popular. NL is a multiple-time High Times Cannabis Cup winner and is one of the parents of other prize-winning strains like Super Silver Haze (SSH), NL#5 x Haze, and the CBD-rich Nordle.

Northern Lights was a cultivar developed during the homegrown revolution of the ‘70s when breeders started developing indica-sativa hybrids to reduce the height of the plant and shorten the flowering time. NL is one of the most popular strains of cannabis available today and is now a mainstay in breeding programs worldwide.

Northern Lights has an earthy, poney flavor and aroma and euphoric, relaxing effects. It is ideal for managing stress, anxiety, insomnia, and chronic pain.
Growing:
Northern Lights grows well both indoors and outdoors, with many choosing to produce this cultivar indoors using the “sea of green” (SoG) method (i.e., finding a mother plant, taking clones from it, and growing several plants in a small grow area). NL generally grows short and stout and flowers quickly, being quite pest-resistant. It is also less sensitive to overfeeding nitrogen than other cannabis strains, making Northern Lights an excellent strain for beginners to grow.

Height

In an indoor setting, expect Northern Lights to grow between 3 and 5 feet, while NL may grow taller in an outdoor environment.

Humidity and Temperature

Northern Lights flourishes in warm, sunny climates with long summer seasons and can grow well in Continental or Mediterranean climates. The ideal temperature is between 70 and 85 degrees Fahrenheit (21 to 29 degrees Celsius).

Northern Lights can tolerate slightly more humid conditions than other cannabis strains, so humidity levels can be between 50% and 60% during the vegetative stage. This should be gradually decreased to between 30%-40% during the flowering stage.

Flowering

7-8 weeks. Outdoors in the Northern Hemisphere, expect Northern Lights to finish around the end of September to mid-October or the end of February to mid-March in the Southern Hemisphere.

Name: Mimosa
Description:
Mimosa, a.k.a. Purple Mimosa, is a sativa-dominant hybrid created by Symbiotic Genetics. It was bred by crossing parents Clementine and Purple Punch. Mimosa hit the scene in 2017 and quickly placed second in the High Times Cannabis Cup in 2018. It is a potent 70% sativa and 30% indica hybrid with an average THC range of 20% to 25%.

Mimosa is a typical “wake and bake” strain (cultivar) ideal for morning use. It has strong cerebral effects, giving users a happy and energetic high, perfect for social situations. Mimosa may help alleviate stress and anxiety, boost energy, and improve focus. This could also make Mimosa useful for managing chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) symptoms or ADHD.

As the name suggests, Mimosa has a fruity flavor profile with sweet and sour tastes. It has a strong citrus scent with a combination of lemon and sweet orange mellowed by an undertone of earthy pine.
Growing:
Mimosa produces beautiful cone-shaped green buds with bright orange pistils. The flowers are heavily coated with bright white trichomes that look like a delicate layer of fresh frost. Mimosa buds are small but densely packed.

Mimosa is a favorite of experienced growers but may be more difficult to grow for beginners. Mimosa is a heavy feeder, and to bring out the best of its cannabinoid and terpene profile, it is recommended to grow this cultivar in a nutrient-rich medium.

If growing in soil, a super soil mix is recommended but be careful not to over-feed these plants as they could still get nutrient burn. If you are growing in a soilless medium with liquid nutrients, it would be beneficial to boost the nitrogen content in the vegetative stage and then boost the phosphorus and potassium levels in the flowering period to promote the growth of the bud sites.

Mimosa is a large plant that does well both indoors and outdoors. It is known to be resistant to pests and diseases common to cannabis. Mimosa is a relatively consistent strain with little mention of various phenotypes. It responds well to “screen of green” (SCROG) training.

The SCROG method involves topping the plants in the early vegetative stage (removing the apical or center stem). This encourages the plant to produce more side shoots, eventually becoming colas (flowers). Once topped, the branches of the plants are gently weaved through support (usually a horizontal trellis) to maximize the amount of light reaching each potential bud site.

It will be important to top this plant if growing indoors as it can reach heights above 80 inches indoors. With good training, Mimosa will produce numerous well-developed colas and yield approximately 400 grams per square meter indoors and 500 grams outdoors.

Height

Mimosa can reach up to 90 inches outdoors and between 60-80 inches indoors.

Humidity and Temperature

Mimosa can tolerate cooler temperatures than some cannabis plants but protects it from frost if growing outdoors. When growing Mimosa, keep the relative humidity between 40% to 60% in the vegetative phase, and drop it to 30% to 40% during flowering to prevent molds such as bud rot from taking hold. Temperatures should stay at 70 to 80 degrees Fahrenheit (21 to 26 degrees Celsius).

Flowering

Mimosa takes anywhere from 68 to 78 days to flower, approximately nine weeks.

Name: Lavender
Description:
A Soma Seeds creation, Lavender — sometimes called Lavender Kush — is an indica-dominant hybrid strain (cultivar) bred from four parents: Super Skunk, Big Skunk Korean, Afghani, and Hawaiian. Lavender produces dense buds with a moderate THC content, typically between 14% and 20%. It may not be the most potent strain, but it’s nonetheless reported to alleviate chronic pain while providing strong cerebral effects.

On the nose, Lavender flower aptly smells like lavender flowers, and some describe its aroma as a sensually spicy smell. The strain’s most ardent fans claim Lavender’s leaves sport one of the darkest purple colorations among cannabis plants (a byproduct of the presence of a group of flavonoids called anthocyanins). However, several strains exhibit similar purple hues.

Celebrated for a relatively short flowering cycle of eight to 10 weeks, Lavender is an easy strain (cultivar) for beginners to grow due to its resistance to various environmental conditions. But because it can grow up to 8 feet tall, cultivators must be prepared to accommodate the plant with the space it needs to thrive.
Growing:
Those interested in cultivating Lavender must consider that this strain requires a lot of room to thrive. It’s common for mature plants to reach or exceed 8 feet in height. But with ample space, Lavender can be successfully grown indoors, outdoors, or in a greenhouse and will reward its cultivators with signature purple hues. Its ideal harvest month is October if grown outdoors.

Height

Lavender reportedly grows between 6-8 feet tall. Those looking to manage the height of their plants due to space restrictions and confidentiality may wish to grow a variety like Lavender using the sea of green (SoG) method. That is, selecting a mother plant and taking cuttings from the mother to grow smaller clones, which should only grow to a maximum of a few feet.

Humidity and Temperature

Lavender thrives in temperate, sunny climates, so maintaining temperatures between 70 and 80 degrees Fahrenheit is ideal. Keep relative humidity levels between 50% and 60% during its seedling phase, after which humidity levels should remain between 40% and 50%.

Flowering

Lavender’s flowering time is typically between eight and 10 weeks.

Name: Larry OG
Description:
Larry OG, also known as Lemon Larry and Grandpa Larry, is a balanced indica-sativa hybrid with a tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) content between 22% and 24.5% and a cannabidiol (CBD) content between 0.57% and 0.72%. Its moderately high THC content and relaxing yet uplifting effects suggest that Larry OG may be useful for managing chronic pain, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and, in moderate doses, depression.

The strain is a member of the famous ocean-grown lineage and was developed by crossing the hybrid OG Kush with an indica SFV OG Kush from the San Fernando Valley. Larry OG has won several awards, including the Best Hybrid award in 2012 and the Best Medicinal Strain award in the 2014 Denver Cannabis Cup.
Growing:
Larry OG plants have dense buds and long pistils with a burnt orange color.

This strain is relatively easy to grow and is resistant to common molds and mildew. It can be grown both indoors and outdoors but prefers indoors, where it can be grown in soil or hydroponics setups. Heavy feeding schedules are recommended. Growers have reported indoor cannabis yields of 19 ounces per square meter when grown indoors and 16 ounces per plant (450 grams per plant) outdoors.

Height

Larry OG plants grow quite tall, up to 80 inches (2 meters). If you are trying to grow it indoors, it may need topping. Topping involves pruning the top part of the main stem of the plant, which stops it from continuing to grow taller and encourages the growth of side branches instead.

Humidity and Temperature

When grown outdoors, Larry OG prefers low humidity climates with temperatures between 68 and 80 degrees Fahrenheit (20-27 degrees Celsius).

Flowering

The typical indoor flowering time of Larry OG is around eight weeks. When grown outdoors, Larry OG flowers in late summer and is normally ready for harvest by October.

Kosher Tangie Kush, also known as 24k Gold, is an indica-dominant hybrid strain that is a cross between Kosher Kush and Tangie. Some enthusiasts argue that it is a blend of Kosher Kush and Tangerine Dream. Kosher Tangie Kush is known for its high THC content, which averages around 20% but can reach up to 24%. The strain is composed of 60% indica and 40% sativa.

Kosher Tangie Kush is renowned for its uplifting and relaxing effects, making it a favorite among cannabis users. However, beginners should proceed with caution due to its potent psychoactive properties. The high THC content in Kosher Tangie Kush may make it beneficial for those dealing with stress, depression, and chronic pain. The strain is characterized by its unique flavor profile, which combines the sweetness of citrus fruits with the earthy undertones of kush, resulting in a taste that is both tangy and rich.
Growing:
Kosher Tangie Kush plants are moderately challenging to grow, reaching a medium height with a substantial yield. Suitable for both indoor and outdoor cultivation, this strain is an ideal option for intermediate and experienced growers.

Height

Kosher Tangie Kush plants are moderately tall, boasting sturdy stems. Given proper care, cultivators can expect a bountiful yield.

Humidity and Temperature

The Kosher Tangie Kush strain flourishes most effectively in a moderately warm climate. Cultivating indoors allows growers to regulate the ideal temperature and humidity levels.

Flowering

The flowering time for Kosher Tangie Kush is moderate, typically around nine to ten weeks.

Name: Key Lime Pie
Description:
The Key Lime Pie marijuana strain is an indica hybrid strain that is a gourmet phenotype of GSC bred in California by Burnish Bush Nurseries. The plant crosses OG Kush, Durban Poison, and Cherry Pie and has lime candy, mint, and spicy flavors that leave an earthy and chocolatey aftertaste.

Some have suggested the potent strain crosses Sour Diesel, OG Kush, and Granddaddy Purple, implying Afghani, Nepalese, and Thai origins.

The body effects of Key Lime Pie leave users feeling quite spaced out, and a bit “couch locked,” which lends it to use in the late afternoon to evening. Its high is mellowing even though it has high THC content and very little CBD content.
Growing:
The Key Lime Pie plant has strong indica characteristics with small- to medium-sized buds that adhere in nugget-like shapes and leaves of bright green. The buds often have purple hues due to being grown in colder temperatures.

The plant is relatively easy to grow inside and outside but prefers temperatures between 70 and 80 degrees Fahrenheit. Key Lime Pie seeds are not commercially available, and the strain must be grown as a clone from clippings.

Height

The Key Lime Pie plant reaches between 60 and 80 inches tall regardless of whether it is grown indoors or outdoors, with similar yields in both conditions. There are several tips and tricks that you can use to increase yield.

Humidity and Temperature

This plant is especially resilient to different conditions but is ideally kept between 70% and 80% humidity at first. This can be reduced when it begins to flower to prevent the buds from rotting.

Flowering

It takes between nine and 10 weeks for this plant to flower when grown indoors, and it can be harvested from early October when grown outdoors. There are several different ways to tell if your plant has been flowering for long enough to be harvested.

Name: Kandy Kush
Description:
Kandy Kush — aka Candy Kush — is an indica-dominant hybrid bred by DNA Genetics. It crosses the classic kush strain, OG Kush and Trainwreck. Hailing from two California greats, Kandy Kush is an award-winning strain (cultivar) with a THC concentration of 14% to 18%.

Kandy Kush is a great evening strain with strong relaxing effects allowing users to wind down after a long day. Kandy Kush may be ideal for alleviating stress, anxiety, and insomnia.

Kandy Kush has a sweet lemon scent and sweet candy flavor with herbal and peppery undertones. The hybrid strain’s indica effects, aroma, and great taste are some of the reasons it won the top spot in the 1st Annual Western Slope Cannabis Crown.
Growing:
Kandy Kush produces densely-packed buds with beautiful green and purple hues thanks to its trainwreck parents. This variety branches well and can produce around 400 grams per square meter when grown indoors.

Kandy Kush is known to have multiple phenotypes. A squat and bushy plant typical of indica lineages is the most common, but taller sativa-type phenotypes are also known. Both phenotypes have approximately the same flowering time.

The compact phenotype may be more suitable for beginner growers as compact plants are generally easier to manage in terms of training and trimming; however, it will still be essential to keep on top of trimming the fan leaves of the compact variety to let light into bud sites deeper in the plant and improve air circulation.

Both phenotypes are well-suited for “screen of green” (SCROG) training, and it may be necessary to train your plants this way for the taller phenotype if your indoor setup is small. The SCROG method involves topping the plants in the early vegetative stage (removing the apical or center stem).

This encourages the plant to produce more side-shoots, eventually becoming colas (flowers). Once topped, the branches of the plants are gently weaved through support (usually a horizontal trellis) to maximize the amount of light reaching each potential bud site.

Low-stress training (LST) may also work well for Kandy Kush. Similar to the SCROG method, LST is used to increase plant yield. Plants are topped to encourage lateral outgrowths tied down towards the pot, typically with string, to spread branches out horizontally and maximize light penetration. This method does not require trellising.

Height

The most common Kandy Kush phenotype is short and stocky, typically reaching about 14 inches (60 cm). This phenotype is well-suited to indoor environments and may not need much training to stay manageable. The sativa-dominant phenotype may grow taller, and it would be advisable to train it if growing indoors.

Humidity and Temperature

Kandy Kush is suited to growing in cooler environments, but make sure you avoid frosts.
When growing Kandy Kush, keep the relative humidity between 40%-60% in the vegetative phase and drop it to 30%-40% during flowering to prevent molds such as bud rot from taking hold. Try to keep the temperature range between 70-80 F.

Flowering

Kandy Kush has a longer flowering time than some other varieties, taking around 67 to 73 days to mature indoors. Kandy Kush is known to be mold and pest resistant, so if managed well, this extra growth time shouldn’t pose too much of a threat to yields.
You may be able to find auto-flowering varieties of Kandy Kush, which will flower automatically with age rather than from a change in lighting. It’s important to note that these varieties have been crossed and may not produce a true Kandy Kush phenotype.

Name: Jager
Description:
Jager (Jagermeister, Jager Kush, JGR) is an indica-dominant strain created by an unidentified breeder from southern Oregon. Its lineage is also slightly mysterious, but it’s thought that its genetics come from a cross between LA Confidential and Blue Dream. Jager is an 80% indica, 20% sativa strain (cultivar) with a THC content between 19% and 22%.

Jager is a classic “couch lock” strain with strong sedative and relaxing effects. It may help relieve chronic pain, muscle spasms, and tremors. This strain is recommended for nighttime use, assisting people in easing into blissful sleep.

Jager is noted for its sweet berry flavor and black licorice aroma, similar to the German liquor Jagermeister.
Growing:
Jager produces long, tapered buds with fiery orange hairs (pistils) and dark green leaves with deep rich purple undertones.

This strain is suitable for beginner growers as it is compact and resistant to mold, which can quickly destroy a cannabis crop if unmanaged. This strain is short and squat, requiring a certain degree of trimming to improve light penetration and air circulation; however, it may not need excessive training to be manageable.

It is a smaller variety with modest yields of up to 200 grams per square meter indoors. Topping Jager (removing the middle stem) is recommended to encourage the plant to increase branching and eventual bud production.

Height

Both indoor and outdoor, Jager is less than 30 inches tall.

Humidity and Temperature

Jager prefers a humid outdoor environment. When growing indoors, keep the relative humidity between 40%-60% in the vegetative phase and drop it to 30%-40% during flowering to prevent molds. Temperatures should stay between 70-80 F (21-26 C). Humidity may fluctuate; continual humidity monitoring is essential.

Flowering

Jager takes approximately 45-50 days to flower (six to seven weeks). This makes it an ideal strain for beginners.

Name: Jack Herer
Description:
Also known as The Jack, Platinum Jack, JH, and Premium Jack, Jack Herer is a famous strain of 55% sativa and 45% indica, enabling it to create balanced cerebral and bodily effects. Believed to be a cross between a Haze hybrid and a Northern Lights #5 and Shiva Skunk hybrid, its tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) content is between 15% and 24%, and its cannabidiol (CBD) content is around 0.7%-1.0%. Jack Herer is noted for its uplifting effects and could help manage anxiety, depression, and chronic pain.

The strain was named in honor of the real Jack Herer, a famous cannabis rights campaigner who passed away in 2010. He was affectionately known as “The Hemperor,” or “The Emperor of Hemp” and was the author of the Hemp Bible and The Emperor Wears No Clothes.

Jack Herer’s aroma is much prized and properly cured. Jack Herer strain flowers have a citrus bouquet. This plant releases an herbal scent similar to sage when burned, and the smoke also has an herbal taste, with some users describing the overall impression as similar to potpourri.

Since Jack Herer’s development in the Netherlands in the 1990s, it’s become a staple strain of cannabis for many people. It is famous around the world both for recreational and medicinal use. It has won nine Cannabis Cup titles, including first place for sativa in 1999.

Jack Herer genetics have since been used to develop several other strains, including Pineapple Jack, Jack’s Cleaner, Critical Jack, Jack Skellington, and Jack Flash.
Growing:
In terms of appearance, Jack Herer plants have dark green leaves and dark orange pistils. The plant produces large quantities of trichomes and sticky resin, and it’s considered a sparkling and crystalline strain.

Jack Herer is one of the most widely available strains. It can be grown outdoors or indoors. If grown outdoors, it prefers a Mediterranean-type climate. It’s highly resistant to diseases, molds, and pests. It should be fed lightly with essential nutrients to prevent burn.

Silica-based foods are best as they allow the plant to grow large, thick stems to support the weight of the big, dense buds. Yield-wise, growers can expect a single square meter of this strain to produce up to 18 ounces (510 g) per square meter when grown indoors and 18 ounces per plant outdoors.

Height

Jack Herer plants grow up to 6.5 feet (2 meters) tall, which is taller than most strains of cannabis. This means they may require topping if grown indoors. Topping involves pruning the top of the main stem off the plant, stopping it from growing too tall and instead promoting lateral branches’ growth, making the plant shorter and bushier overall.

Humidity and Temperature

Jack Herer prefers a growing temperature between 70 and 80 degrees Fahrenheit or 21-27 degrees Celsius.

Flowering

Jack Herer strain typically takes eight to 10 weeks to flower if grown indoors. If grown outdoors, it should flower between late September and early October.

Name: Jack Frost
Description:
Jack Frost is a hybrid marijuana strain produced by crossing the following three strains together:

An additional cannabis strain called Rainbow Kashmiri (Rainbow Kush) is also sometimes included in the mix, but this is less common.

The sweet, woody, skunky, and citrus flavor profile contributes to the creativity-boosting, happy and energizing body effects of Jack Frost. This makes a cultivar like Jack Frost potentially helpful in managing anxiety, depression, stress, and chronic fatigue.

Jack Frost was developed and perfected by the Californian brand Goldenseed over five years. It is a sativa-dominant strain, containing 65% Cannabis sativa and 35% Cannabis indica genetics.

Jack Frost is named after the crystallized layers of frosty-looking white trichomes present on the buds of the plant. Some say they resemble Christmas trees, and bright orange pistils also characterize the plant. Overall, Jack Frost has a fluffy, dry, and delicate appearance.
Growing:
Jack Frost plants are relatively easy to grow for beginners and veteran growers. It doesn’t require as much attention as other strains, as it’s resistant to most molds, mildew, pests, and diseases.

Jack Frost can be successfully grown indoors or outdoors.

Some cultivators say that it’s best to grow Jack Frost in soil. However, a hydroponics setup can be used if desired. This is where cannabis plants are grown in a nutrient-rich water solution rather than soil.

Both the “sea of green” (growing many small plants in a small confined area) and the “screen of green” (manipulating the branches to grow horizontally to expose more to the light) growing methods can be applied to Jack Frost.

Jack Frost plants produce an average-sized yield. When grown indoors, you can expect one plant to produce a yield of approximately 16 ounces (453 grams) of bud per square meter. When grown outdoors, a yield of about 19 ounces (548 grams) per square meter can be expected.

Height

Sativa-dominant strains are usually tall. You can expect your Jack Frost plants to reach between 60 and 80 inches (1.5 to 2 meters).

Humidity and Temperature

A sunny, warm and dry climate is preferred for growing Jack Frost plants. Humidity should be kept between 40% to 50%. The optimal temperature is from 68 to 78 degrees Fahrenheit (20 to 26 degrees Celsius).

Flowering

Jack Frost plants generally take eight to nine weeks to flower. If you grow them outdoors, they should be ready to harvest by the end of September or early October in the Northern Hemisphere.

Name: Hog
Description:
The Hog marijuana strain is a pure (100%) indica cultivar with a secretive past. Breeders at T.H. Seeds in Amsterdam have kept the genetic lineage of this strain to themselves. It also goes by the names Haracept and Tennessee Hog.

Hog first placed in the indica strain category at the 2002 High Times Cannabis Cup. It’s renowned for its strong sedative effects, reserved for well-seasoned cannabis users. Hog is an ideal variety of cannabis for managing chronic pain and insomnia.

Hog is said to be one of the most potent strains in the world, with high THC levels varying from 17% to 29% and a stinky, sour pungency.
Growing:
Hog is a great option for novice growers as it isn’t too challenging to look after due to its thick and sturdy nature. This strain has a short flowering time and offers a high yield of around 27 ounces per plant (400-600 grams per square meter), making it an even more attractive option for experienced growers and novices alike.

Buds have a classically dense indica structure, some with hints of orange and purple. It may need occasional pruning to keep side branches under control, preventing excess moisture from seeping in and helping to aerate the plant.

Something to keep in mind is that this strain has a very potent smell, so you may need some control measures to stop the smell from taking over.

Height

Hog is a short plant that grows to around 3-4.5 feet (100-140 centimeters). This makes it a great option if you’re looking for an easy strain to grow indoors.

Humidity and Temperature

Hog grows best in a Mediterranean environment. Start with a humidity of around 70% during the seedling stage. As you near the flowering stage, lower this humidity to 40%. This is critical because if you keep humidity high, you risk more moisture trapped in your buds, leading to mold growth.

Flowering

Flowering time is shorter than many other strains, at eight weeks. For cannabis to enter the flowering stage requires periods of 10-12 hours of complete darkness, so keep this in mind if you’re growing indoors. The flowering stage will occur naturally outdoors as the days get shorter.

Name: Hindu Kush
Description:
The Hindu Kush strain is a pure indica landrace cannabis strain from the Hindu Kush mountain range, spanning Afghanistan and Pakistan. This strain is known for its potent effects, distinct earthy aroma, and THC levels ranging from 15% to 20%, with minimal CBD content.

The Hindu Kush strain boasts a unique and complex flavor profile, featuring earthy, sweet, spicy, and floral notes that create a delightful sensory experience for users. The aroma of this strain is equally captivating, with its earthy and pungent scent that intensifies as the buds are broken apart and ground, releasing subtle hints of pine and skunk.

Hindu Kush is a 100% indica strain renowned for its powerful and long-lasting effects, providing a balanced experience for recreational and medical marijuana users. The potent effects of this strain make it an ideal choice for those looking to relieve symptoms of various medical conditions, such as depression, anxiety, appetite loss, insomnia, and nausea.
Growing:
The Hindu Kush strain is well-suited for indoor and outdoor cultivation, with a preference for a warm climate. It is relatively easy to grow, making it suitable for novice and experienced growers. Hindu Kush seeds can be obtained from reputable seed banks and germinated before planting.

During the vegetative stage, Hindu Kush plants require ample light and nutrients to support their growth. This stage typically lasts about four to six weeks, during which the plants develop a robust root system, sturdy branches, and large fan leaves. It is essential to provide the plants with the right conditions, lighting, temperature, and humidity, to ensure a healthy vegetative stage.

Height

The Hindu Kush strain typically grows to a medium height, reaching around four to six feet tall. This makes it an ideal choice for indoor growers with limited space and outdoor growers who prefer a more manageable plant size.

The strain can yield up to 14 ounces per square meter when grown indoors and up to 16 ounces per plant outdoors. To maximize the yield, it is essential to provide the plants with the right conditions throughout their growth cycle, including adequate lighting, proper nutrients, and optimal temperature and humidity levels.

Humidity and Temperature

The Hindu Kush strain prefers a warm and dry climate, with temperatures ranging from 70-80°F and moderate humidity levels. Maintaining the ideal temperature and humidity levels is crucial for the health and productivity of the plants. Excessive humidity can lead to mold and mildew issues, while extreme temperatures can cause stress and negatively affect the plants’ growth and yield.

Flowering

The flowering time for the Hindu Kush strain is approximately seven to nine weeks. During this stage, the plants will start producing tiny hairs, or pistils, eventually developing into dense, resinous buds. It is crucial to monitor the plants closely during this stage, provide the necessary nutrients, and maintain the ideal temperature and humidity levels to ensure a successful harvest.

Name: Headband
Description:
Headband, commonly known as HB, is a hybrid marijuana strain (cultivar). Headband has been reported as having euphoric, uplifting, and stimulating effects, with some even finding a boost in creativity. This means that Headband may help manage stress, fatigue, and depression.

A cross between the famous staple strains OG Kush and Sour Diesel, the parents have passed on their high THC content to Headband, which can reach a THC level of 27%. Some suggest that Master Kush is one of Headband’s parents as well.

HB is known for its creaminess and lemon and diesel flavors. Celebrated for its relaxation, stress, and pain relief effects, it is a favorite among cannabis users.

HB is a potent strain: The strain’s THC content is 27%, with little-to-no CBD. It’s a well-balanced, indica-dominated (55%-60%) hybrid.

Some users experience pressure feeling around the top of their heads, which may feel like a headband. This is where the strain gets its name.

Because the THC levels in this strain are so high, it produces a sensation of pressure on the temples. This is because it dilates the blood vessels in the face, and THC is therefore considered a vasodilator.

Some believe Headband was created by Reserva Privada, a breeder from Colorado known for creating extremely popular strains like Kandy Kush and Strawberry Banana. Others believe the headband strain originates in Humboldt County, part of the well-known Emerald Triangle.

Be sure to pace yourself, as the effects of HB can take some time to kick in.
Growing:
Headband is surprisingly easy to grow, even for people new to cultivating cannabis. The hardy indica plants are relatively bushy and shorter than the average plant.
The HB plants will thrive with the proper trimming and light conditions. They can even survive temperature changes so that they can be suitable as both indoor and outdoor plants.
However, growers should note that Headband cannabis plants can have an intense aroma, so be sure to have odor regulation measures in place to prevent leaking odors.

Height

HB plants are generally shorter than other strains and quite bushy. Expect plants to grow up to 80 inches tall.

Humidity and Temperature

Humidity is also essential — maintain a humidity level between 50%-70%.

Flowering

To induce flowering, growers need to mimic a seasonal change. To do this, alter the light schedule, so the plants are in darkness for 12 hours and light for 12 hours.
The flowering stage will take around eight to 12 weeks. For HB, this is usually nine to 10 weeks.
When they have reached the harvesting stage, the HB plants will have about 70% of the pistils a reddish/brown color. This is the pistil method.
The trichome method relies on a color change in the trichomes — when they are milky white or cloudy in color, they are ready to harvest. It is best to leave them when they are still transparent until the trichomes change.

Name: GSC
Description:
GSC is an indica-dominant strain (variety) of cannabis and is a cross between OG Kush and Durban Poison. It is approximately 60% Cannabis indica and 40% Cannabis sativa. GSC flowers usually have been measured to contain around 19% to 20% THC, very little CBD, and occasionally about 1% CBG. Due to the Durban Poison parentage, some varieties may contain THCV.

GSC were bred and developed by the Cookie Fam collective in San Francisco and released around 2009. Rumors suggest that the original breeder is Berner, but this has not been confirmed. Popular hybrids include Animal Cookies, Platinum Cookies, Thin Mint, Blue Cookies, Gelato, and Cookies n Cream.

The exact lineage of the strain is also unknown and is kept a secret among members of the collective, who have also bred cultivars like Gelato, Cherry Pie, and Sunset Sherbet. GSC’s parents are thought to be Florida OG Kush and F1 Durban Poison, and Granddaddy Purple (GDP) may also be one of the parents.

The GSC strain is noted for its sweet, mint, vanilla, biscuit, chocolate, and pastry-like flavors and appetite-inducing, uplifting effects. Patients have used GSC for chronic pain, nausea, appetite loss, anxiety, and depression.
Growing:
GSC has grown in popularity over the years. As with many other popular cannabis strains, many producers create copies or approximations of the genetics (often called “hacks”) to sell seeds. Some of these may be good copies, some less so. You can get GSC either as a clone from a dispensary in states that allow for cultivation or seed from Cali Connection.

Those looking for a high-yielding cannabis variety may want to consider another strain, as GSC’s yield is moderate, or approximately 10 ounces per square meter when grown indoors using the “sea of green” (SoG) method (considered ideal). Those looking to maximize yield ought to think about training their plant.

GSC is usually recommended for growers with some experience. Indoor or greenhouse grows are ideal for this variety of cannabis, and it is best to find a good mother plant, take cuttings and grow from clones.

Height

GSC usually grow to a height between 30 and 60 inches (2.5 to 5 feet), depending on the phenotype. As GSC contains a strong sativa component, some may grow towards the taller end of the range.

Humidity and Temperature

During the vegetative period, GSC prefers a temperature of about 68 to 77 degrees Fahrenheit (20 to 25 degrees Celsius) and 50% humidity. During the flowering stage, a similar temperature of 68 to 80 degrees Fahrenheit (20 to 26 degrees Celsius) during the day is generally optimal, falling to between 60 to 70 degrees Fahrenheit (15.5 to 21 degrees Celsius) at night. It is best to reduce the humidity in your grow room to 30% during the flowering stage.

Flowering

GSC take around about 9 to 10 weeks to finish flowering

Name: Green Crack
Description:
Green Crack, also known as Green Cush, Green Crush, or Mango Crack, is a sativa-dominant cannabis strain that is known for its energizing effects. Green Crack is a cross between Skunk #1 and an indica of unknown lineage and is 65% sativa and 35% indica. THC levels vary between 13% and 21%, averaging around 17%. Some suggest that Green Crack contains THCV as well.

Green Crack contains little CBD, measuring at around 0.2%. However, a CBD Green Crack strain crosses Green Crack and California Orange CBD and has a THC:CBD ratio of 1:2 (6% THC, 12% CBD).

Green Crack has a mango, tropical, and citrus flavor profile. Due to its effects, it may help manage ADHD, depression, anxiety, and stress. Although generally a sativa, there can be indica-dominant phenotypes, which could have more sedative effects.
Growing:
Green Crack is usually a tall, lanky sativa that likes to grow outdoors in sunny, Mediterranean climates, where it can yield up to 20 ounces per plant. Green Crack does well indoors as well, and can yield 18 ounces per square meter using the “sea of green” (SoG) method. To reduce height in indoor settings, you may elect to use the “screen of green” (ScrOG) method and choose a more indica-dominant phenotype as the mother plant. Green Crack can do especially well in a greenhouse setting.

Compared to many other sativa-dominant varieties, Green Crack can flower in as little as eight weeks. However, Green Crack can be quite sensitive to nutrients, temperature and humidity, so it is not necessarily recommended for beginner gardeners. Green Crack requires a higher amount of phosphorus than usual during the pre-flower stage, and you will want to be careful of over-watering and humidity levels in order to prevent mold and bud rot.

Height

Expect Green Crack to grow between 3 and 9 feet tall.

Humidity and Temperature

Green Crack does well in temperatures between 70 and 90 degrees Fahrenheit (21 to 32 degrees Celsius), so this variety of cannabis can handle slightly higher temperatures compared to many others.

A humidity level of 50% in your grow room or space is ideal during the vegetative stage, but Green Crack is quite sensitive to humidity and over-watering, so you will want to ensure that the humidity is about 30% during flowering.

Flowering

Eight to nine weeks

Name: Grape Ape
Description:
The Grape Ape strain is an indica-dominant hybrid strain from Apothecary Genetics that’s popular with users who enjoy a fruity aroma. As the name suggests, the Grape Ape strain exhibits dominant grape flavors, and other notes include candy and strawberry flavors.

It crosses three popular strains: Mendocino Purps, Skunk, and Original Afghani. Its THC levels test at around 20%, while its CBD content is practically nonexistent (0-1%). The relatively high THC levels give users an enjoyable mind and body high, making it a popular strain for recreational use.
Growing:
This strain can be a challenging strain for novice growers to work with. However, for beginners or experienced growers, it can be successfully grown both inside and outside. The Grape Ape strain produces a small bushy plant with a beautiful purple color.

Height

Being of indica nature, it does not grow extremely tall, making it an ideal indoor plant, and the Grape Ape strain rarely exceeds 4 feet in height. However, it grows pretty dense and requires trimming to avoid bud rot, which many find challenging.

Humidity and Temperature

Bud rot is a mold that targets various cannabis plants and can kill them. The risk of bud rot developing is increased if the plant is kept in highly humid conditions with poor ventilation. The plant is, therefore, best kept at lower humidity levels, ideally around 50% when it is growing and at even lower humidity (30%-40%) when flowering.
Adequate ventilation is essential to help achieve this, especially if the plant is grown indoors. Trimming the plant can be a useful way to increase circulation to the inner part of the plant, mainly because indica strains, like this one, tend to be highly dense.

Flowering

The Grape Ape strain’s harvest time is sometime between October and September, depending on the conditions it’s grown in. Its flowering time is between seven to eight weeks. During this time, growers can enjoy a relatively high yield of 28 ounces per plant.

Name: Granddaddy Purple
Description:
The indica-dominant Granddaddy Purple strain crosses the classic Purple Urkle and Big Bud strains. This popular cannabis strain is highly sought-after for its deeply relaxing and soothing effects. With a high THC content of around 23%, the Granddaddy Purple strain is a potent option for those seeking a powerful experience.

The flavor profile of Granddaddy Purple is a delightful mix of sweet, fruity, and earthy notes with a distinct grape taste. The aroma is equally enticing, boasting a complex blend of rich berry, earthy, and slightly skunky scents.

Thanks to its 70% indica and 30% sativa composition, the Granddaddy Purple strain is an excellent choice for recreational and medical marijuana users. Its cerebral euphoria and uplifting qualities can help alleviate stress and anxiety, while its deeply relaxing effects can aid in combating insomnia and promoting restful sleep. Additionally, the strain’s ability to stimulate appetite may benefit those experiencing appetite loss or dealing with the side effects of certain medical treatments.
Growing:
The Grandaddy Purple strain is suitable for indoor and outdoor cultivation, with a preference for a warm and dry climate. This short, compact plant is an excellent choice for small spaces, making it a popular option for novice and experienced growers.

Height

The Grandaddy Purple strain typically grows to two to three feet, making it a compact and manageable plant for indoor cultivation. It’s also known for its high yield, with indoor growers typically producing up to 500 grams per square meter and outdoor growers yielding up to 17 ounces per plant.

Humidity and Temperature

The Grandaddy Purple strain prefers a warm and dry climate, with temperatures between 70-80°F and humidity levels around 50%.

Flowering

The flowering time for the Grandaddy Purple strain is approximately eight to 11 weeks, with outdoor harvests typically occurring in mid-October.

Name: Gorilla Cookies
Description: Gorilla Cookies is a sativa-dominant hybrid of Thin Mint GSC (GSC) and Gorilla Glue #4. The plant produces extremely dense, resinous buds with a THC content ranging from 18% to 28%. Gorilla Cookies has a cool, earthy scent with a hint of sweetness. Gorilla Cookies has been described as having calming, relaxing, sleepy, and giggly effects, which could make this strain (cultivar) ideal for managing anxiety, chronic pain, and insomnia.
Growing:
Gorilla Cookies is a high-yield, high-potency crop suitable for those with little experience growing cannabis. It takes 10 weeks to grow from seed to harvest, with yields of around 1.6-2.0 ounces per square foot when grown indoors and 2-11 ounces per plant when grown outdoors.

It is quite tolerant to variation in temperature, growing well between 60 and 75 degrees Fahrenheit and tolerating temperatures up to 85 degrees Fahrenheit or higher. The strain is also quite forgiving of the pH range it’s grown in, preferring a pH of 5.5 to 6.0 when grown hydroponically and between 6.0 and 7.0 in soil.

A high terpene profile makes Gorilla Cookies more resistant to mold and fungi, allowing the plant to tolerate damper, colder conditions than other strains. However, the highest quality buds are produced when the plant is kept around 70 degrees Fahrenheit and in moderately humid conditions.

Gorilla Cookies also requires some training to produce a substantial crop. The plant can be topped, but this strain is best trained in the low-stress training (LST) method. LST involves bending the plant’s main stem horizontally while the plant is still young and flexible to encourage the growth of side branches.

Height

Whether LST, topping or no training has been done, plants can grow from between 30 and 40 inches. It should be noted that the plant tends to grow very wide and may require some support for longer branches.

Humidity and Temperature

Gorilla Cookies prefers a humidity of around 60%-70% during the first four weeks and 45%-55% for the remaining six weeks. If the plant is grown in temperatures above 85 degrees Fahrenheit, the humidity should be increased accordingly.

Flowering

Gorilla Cookies flowers at around nine to 10 weeks when grown indoors. The plant should be ready for harvest in early September to early October if grown outdoors.
